#1887. Manchester United: Sir Alex Ferguson has already approved of Mauricio Pochettino as talks planned

Mauricio Pochettino says he will have the opportunity to speak to Sir Alex Ferguson as his Manchester United tenure gets underway.

Pochettino was announced as the new Man United head coach on Friday, succeeding Michael Carrick who had been sacked the day before, with the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

However, the Argentine has not yet officially started work at Old Trafford.

As communicated in Man Utd’s official statement, Pochettino has been allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and their double-header against Haiti.

The first of which took place on Saturday evening with USA recording a 6-0 win to put one foot in the CONCACAF Nations League finals.

Following Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge of USA, he spoke to the Telegraph and was asked if he can spoken to Ferguson since accepting the Man United job.

“Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,” the 54-year-old said.

“I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

“For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense. But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.”

Pochettino and Ferguson have remained in close contact since first dining with each other in 2016.

They first crossed paths in the dugout during the 2012-13 season when Man United beat Southampton at Old Trafford, though Pochettino left a lasting impression on Ferguson despite the defeat.

"For the first 30 minutes we were fantastic," Ferguson told BBC Sport in January 2013. "But in the second half Southampton have been the best team to play here this season. We were fortunate to win."

Then in 2016, David Lammy, MP for Tottenham, shared details of a meeting with Ferguson at a charity function.

"I’m going to let you in to a secret," Lammy told The Spurs Show podcast. "About six weeks ago I sat next to Alex Ferguson at a dinner in support of grassroots football abroad.

"He said to me, 'I think you guys have the best manager in the Premier League.' Alex Ferguson said that."

#1885. Arsenal: Why Kepa Arrizabalaga was allowed to make second international debut amid surprise twist

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga has been in action during the international break, though not for the Spain national team.

The 32-year-old, who joined the Gunners from London rivals Chelsea in July 2025 for £5million, has 13 senior caps for La Roja, but has not made an appearance since a 2-0 loss to Scotland in March 2023.

Overlooked once again by Luis de la Fuente for Spain’s Nations League double-header against the Czech Republic and England in favour of Unai Simon, Joan Garcia and Arsenal team-mate David Raya, it was set to be a quiet international window for Kepa.

In a surprise turn of events, Kepa was called up to the Basque Country squad for their friendly against Venezuela and made his debut on Saturday, playing 45 minutes of the 1-0 win at San Mames.

While Athletic Club star Mikel Jauregizar scored the only goal of the game, some Arsenal fans may have been left wondering why their back-up goalkeeper was able to play for another national team.

Of course, it is well known that FIFA rules state that players cannot switch national teams after they've played three competitive fixtures.

However, despite Kepa winning 13 senior caps for Spain, he was cleared to play for the Basque Country because they are currently not recognised by FIFA.

As such, the win over Venezuela was not an official match, in the eyes of football's governing body.

Nevertheless, Kepa was able to get valuable minutes in his legs, having made just one appearance for Arsenal so far this season - the 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup third round.

Future Kepa appearances for the Basque Country could be in doubt as they have started the process to secure official international status for the national team.

Part of a statement reads: “The Basque Football Federation (EFF-FVF) has revived the process to obtain international official status for the Basque National Team, both men's and women's.

“With this aim, it has approached the Supreme Sports Council and has communicated information about the initiative to the Spanish Football Federation.”

Brazilian legend Ronaldinho will, this afternoon, make his first competitive appearance in more than a decade.

The former Barcelona and AC Milan has not played competitively since featuring for Fluminense in September 2015, though that will change on Sunday as he is confirmed to start for Italian third division side Ravenna against local rivals Forli.

"He will play from the start, there's no doubt," Ravenna boss Andrea Mandorlini told reporters. "Then together we will decide how long he plays.

"He is one of the greatest players of the modern era. And we have to get a result. We always play with three forwards. He will be one of the three."

This will be Ronaldinho’s long-awaited debut for the Serie C side after joining the club in August, with footage emerging on social media over the weekend to prove the 46-year-old has not lost a step.

Ravenna are currently sitting in second place - six points behind leaders Spezia - in the Serie C, Group B table and have won four of their last five matches, including the last three in a row.

Speaking in August after announcing his comeback, Ronaldinho revealed his target was to score his 300th career goal having initially retired on 299.

#1883. Wigan Athletic 2 Barnsley 1: Keeping the faith is tough as Reds hit new low

Barnsley were the ones left dishevelled and on the floor by the end.

A single-digit points haul by the second half of November, their season is currently in pieces. Fifty points seems a long way off.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

These lot will give you a chance is the sentence that every opposing League One manager must surely utter when talk turns to Barnsley.

A well-meaning, nice group of boys who say - and hope to do - the right things, Barnsley don’t last the course, unfortunately.

You don't have to play particularly well to beat them and that is a considerable worry.

They have been in most games this season, but eventually err.

Concentration, physicality and sensing danger are all areas where this group are deficient. A disturbing cocktail. They don’t handle pressure, quite simply and their game management is lamentable.

Barnsley have lost their last five away league matches. Their concession of 17 goals in the second half of games is the joint-worst record in the third tier.

The 23rd-placed Reds, only kept off the bottom by goal difference, are winless in nine league matches since September 2. Autumn, certainly on the league front, has been appalling.

Ahead of kick-off, the Monkees "I’m a Believer" got an airing on the Wigan jukebox. Bob Marley’s classic “Three Little Birds” - a song beloved of Barnsley - did the rounds at the final whistle as Wigan escaped the relegation zone after showing the savvy.

Barnsley should be worried about a number of things, for sure.

As is their manager. Keep the Faith is the motto of the Northern Soul movement - another thing associated with Wigan.

Daniel Stendel was clearly struggling on that count in the immediate aftermath of events on Saturday.

He spoke about holding discussions with Reds majority shareholder/chairman Neerav Parekh. Not necessarily about his own position - not yet, anyway - but endeavouring to find ways to support a playing squad who plainly need help.

It was all a bit unclear. It wasn't to do with bringing in more free agents either.

Then what was it? Discussing what Barnsley need to do in the January transfer window should be top of the agenda. Even if it feels some way in the distance.

Make no mistake, if the Oakwell outfit get the winter window wrong, then there is a pretty high chance that they will be playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79 unfortunately.

‘Probably as good a place as we’ve been’, was Gary Caldwell’s pre-match take on Wigan’s mood ahead of this one.

In fairness, his Barnsley counterpart - in his second spell at the club much like the Scot - could have said the same on the back of two healthy cup wins. The league is a different matter, alas.

It was the former whose side would build momentum.

A relatively even first half had one key moment.

Fraser Murray had delivered a warning with his sweet curler producing a full-stretch parry from Ceiran Slicker.

A few minutes later, the Reds custodian had no chance when Murray again showed delicious technique to bend an unstoppable low shot into the far corner, for his first goal of the campaign. An important one.

How the ball arrived at his feet, with Wigan afforded an ocean of space in the middle of the pitch was poor from a Reds perspective. Latics also fancied it out wide against both Ziyad Larkeche and Jubril Okedina.

On the resumption, Barnsley found a much-needed lifeline in front of their admirable band of stoic supporters. Luca Connell found Reyes Cleary - who worried Wigan for most of the afternoon.

He expertly manufactured space before fizzing over a superb low cross which was buried by Cam McGeehan, backing up in the box.

It was classic wing-play from Cleary to present an opportunity on a plate for McGeehan, who struck his ninth goal of the campaign.

Barnsley had their tails up, but - all the while - there was a nagging feeling about what might happen at the other end. The fears were borne out in appalling fashion.

Morgan Fox hung up a cross which was attacked by Jensen Weir. Larkeche, having a poor game, challenged meekly and Weir couldn’t believe his luck.

His header caught Slicker by surprise at the near post as he could only pat the effort into the net, horribly. And that was that. A scruffy concession in a bedraggled season. Sheffield Wednesday next.

Wigan Athletic: Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett (Trevitt 68), Weir, Power, Mellish; Burrowes (Miller 87), Murray; Saydee (Hogan 67). Substitutes unused: J Walsh, Chilokoa-Mullen, A Harris, Higgins.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche (Reid 87); Connell, Johnson (Richards 56); Yoganathan, McGeehan (Noslin 82), Cleary; Kirk (Brownlie 56). Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, Smith, Alker.

#1882. Alisson, 34, reveals he wants to STAY at Liverpool after rolling back the years against Crystal Palace... but is extending the goalkeeper's contract the right call, asks LEWIS STEELE

Published: 07:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:09 EST, 10 November 2026

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker insists he wants to stay at the club after his contract expires at the end of this season.

The Brazilian, now 34, put in a throwback performance in the Reds’ win at Crystal Palace on Sunday with some fine stops to keep his side in the game at 0-0 before the big-money attackers did their job at the other end.

It came after a period where Alisson has been questioned by fans for a string of errors in what is his final contracted year at the club. And the No1 has now opened up on his future for the first time.

Asked if he wants to stay beyond the end of the season, Alisson said: ‘Yes, in my mind. I’m focused on playing every game but in my mind I’m happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations.

‘But my will is to stay. I’m happy here, my family is happy here. I’m still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that’s my thinking on that.’

Alisson later added that his agent has held talks with the club over a new deal.

The 34-year-old keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window

The keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window, which he admits is a decision taken somewhat beyond his will.

He said: ‘It is beneficial (not going), for sure. You have to use it right because you have a lot of time so if you don’t train, if you don’t prepare, time goes really quick and you need to stay sharp.

‘It’s not that I will sit on the couch for a week and then come back training. I still have to work hard but in my mind I can use the time to relax and be more with my family.

‘It’s a little bit against my will. What I always want is to be with the national team but I understand this is what I have at the moment and I will use this time and take the benefit from the rest.’

Should Liverpool continue in Alisson wonderland?

It is tempting to just say ‘yes’ and end this debate there.

Alisson is still the best goalkeeper Liverpool have on their books and, even though he is maybe not as solid as he once was, the 34-year-old remains one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

Last summer, he flirted with the idea of leaving and seriously considered a move to Juventus. Alisson speaks fluent Italian from his time at AS Roma and held talks with the Turin club over a return.

But Liverpool triggered a clause in his deal to extend his stay by a year. With several big names leaving such as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Curtis Jones, the club did not want another experienced head to depart and leave a leadership vacuum.

They have also spent the last three years succession planning for Alisson’s long-term replacement and have signed a number of goalkeepers for more than £60million combined.

Giorgi Mamardashvili is the most obvious in the pecking order. He has had mixed reviews with fans but the Georgian is appreciated more internally than maybe externally. The club believes he has several levels left to step up.

Lucca Brughmans will join from Belgian side Genk after a £28.3million deal was struck. Liverpool genuinely think he is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him.

Liverpool think Lucca Brughmans - who will join them from Belgian side Genk - is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him

They have also signed highly-rated Armin Pecsi and England youth goalkeeper Zach Trinder from Wolves.

Clearly, the post-Alisson future is sorted, with some of them tipped to go far in the game. But are any of them better than Alisson now? No. Will any of them be better next season? No.

Alisson missed 54 games across the previous two seasons with injury and illness, according to Transfermarkt, but his omission from Brazil camps and a specialised pre-season programme mean the keeper seems to have put his issues behind him. Touch wood.

For that reason, a one-year extension makes sense – for both Alisson and 35-year-old captain Virgil van Dijk. The club will have to face up to a future without both of their defensive stalwarts but, for now, they remain the best in class.

#1881. GdS: The ‘dream’ and two alternatives – Milan draw up three-man centre-back wish list

AC Milan are in the market for a new central defender ahead of the winter window, and three names are on the list.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), Gerry Cardinale wants to give Ruben Amorim at least two signings in January. One of them will be a centre-forward – with Nicolo Tresoldi the ambitious idea at the moment – while the other will be a defender.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With Matteo Gabbia sidelined until well into January and Fikayo Tomori currently injured, Amorim has been juggling an emergency in recent weeks. It was a situation further compounded by an issue that arose for Strahinja Pavlović last week.

Fortunately for Amorim, he has found a capable alternative in the youngster Sankhoun Diawara. Looking ahead, however, the club is considering an addition that could immediately boost the level of the department.

A summer target was Gonçalo Inácio whom Amorim knows well, having coached him for years at Sporting CP. Dialogue with the Lisbon club has continued even during the current period when the transfer window is closed, following the failure to reach an agreement before.

Milan could renew their pursuit soon, though there is currently no consensus regarding his asking price. Furthermore, Inácio is left-footed and has primarily played as an outside centre-back throughout his career.

What the Rossoneri need right now is more of a right-footed player capable of rotating between a wide centre-back role and a central position. While it is true that Gonçalo adapted to the right side under Amorim, there are other candidates who are a more natural fit for that role.

For instance, Ismaelo Ganiou of RC Lens has been on the radar for some time. His contract renewal in August does not necessarily rule out a transfer, although there has been no further contact with the French club since initial discussions in the summer.

Among the new names, 21-year-old Massiré Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise is an intriguing prospect. The Belgian club have also moved quickly to secure their young star with a new contract until 2031. That said, it is not a major obstacle, and the price is around €15m.

On the other hand, we need to sign three or four players and we all know for and in what positions. Five signings would be ideal but that’s not doable.

Get both Ismaelo Ganiou and Massiré Sylla. Leave that portuguese alone.

#1880. Wayne Rooney: Quitting booze helped turn my life around ahead of I’m A Celeb

Sign up to our free weekly newsletter for exclusive competitions, offers and theatre ticket deals

Wayne Rooney has revealed that quitting alcohol has transformed his mental health - and has helped him to lose more than three stone in just six months.

Speaking ahead of entering the jungle in the latest series of I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here!, the former footballer said that his marriage to wife Coleen, is in a “much better place” as a result.

The former England captain said stopping drinking has completely overhauled his lifestyle, and that Coleen has noticed the difference in his appearance, happiness and in their relationship.

Rooney, 41, told The Mail on Sunday: “She’s obviously happy because I think, from a point of view of our marriage, it’s in a better place, in a much happier place. And so that obviously makes a difference.

“So I think, yes, she’s obviously said I look a lot better, but also from a mental point of view, I’m in such a better place as well.”

He added: “Having stopped drinking for almost six months now it does help in terms of your food. I’ve just been eating, to be honest, probably as healthy as I’ve ever eaten over that period, and then training, getting back into a routine of training.

“So obviously it all ties in and all helps. And then I had weight to lose as well. So I think I’m just in a really good place, a really happy place.”

Ahead of the show, Rooney has undergone a dramatic transformation even apart from the weight loss, including a nose job and Invisalign to transform his smile.

The former Manchester United striker has spoken openly in the past about his struggles with alcohol.

Fans of Wayne and Coleen could see that she had grown tired of his wild partying during the fly-on-the-wall documentary, The Real Rooneys.

The couple invited cameras into their home for a year to document the highs and lows of their marriage, with scenes showing the pair arguing over Wayne’s boozy nights out.

He added that he had been impressed by her performance, but would love to go one better by winning the show.

#1879. Di'Shon Bernard goal points to Sheffield Wednesday tweak that can up entertainment levels

Despite the 3-0 scoreline over Plymouth Argyle, Challinor's first league game as Owls manager only really delivered on the first front.

But it would be unreasonable to expect an instant transformation, especially with injuries forcing players into unfamiliar positions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After six games without a win and cup defeats in Challinor's first two matches, Wednesday just needed to get over the line.

But on an afternoon where the football never rivalled Plymouth's orange away kit for brightness, one moment really stood out.

It was born of a mistake, Di'Shon Bernard failing to find Keillor-Dunn after winning the ball deep in Wednesday territory.

But when Malachi Boateng's interception turned into a one-two and the centre-back drove into shooting range and scored in off a post.

The game already won by Keillor-Dunn's finish two minutes earlier, it was no more than the cherry on the cake, six games into Bernard’s return from a 19-month knee injury.

But the story of Henrik Pedersen's tenure was clear – excited by the potential of David Storch’s ownership, Owls fans are greedy. They do not just want the cake, they want the cherries too. After the thin gruel of last season, who can blame them?

"I want people to be brave," said Challinor. "If the shot goes into the Kop, so be it. I'll always encourage people to make positive decisions.

"They're going to make mistakes. We're going to ask them to do things that are different.

"Of course we'll get frustrated, but that's acceptable. That's on us and that will always be the case."

Wednesday's shape flitted between a 4-2-3-1 and a 3-2-4-1 when Sil Swinkels tucked from left-back into a more familiar position.

Back threes need a player willing to break out, especially on days – not Saturday, in fairness – when the visitors come to S6 to frustrate.

"We should, if we do things right, come up against more blocks and teams getting men behind the ball,” argued Challinor.

"That's when people need to step in, be positive and make the most of opportunities. That comes from backing yourself, and quality."

Bernard, a team-mate of Marcus Rashford in the Manchester United youth ranks, has that.

"He wants to put his body on the line," commented Challinor. "He got injured at Notts County by blocking a shot and opening his knee up.

"There's loads of work we can do with him, he can get so much better.

"We'll ask him to be better and more positive in possession as well as being able to do the other things."

When pressed into giving the ball up in the 37th minute he got back to kill the move when it came into the penalty area. When Xavier Amaechi threatened to force his way through, Bernard refused to be shaken off and made an excellent recovery tackle.

He believes working with Challinor and his assistant Clint Hill – more no-nonsense centre-backs in their day – can elevate his game.

"Playing the right of a three he's trusting me to do more on the ball," he says. "Before I got injured, that was probably one of my strengths.

"Now I need to really just build up the confidence to do more of it because you can see in glimpses I am capable of it.

"He's pushing me to be that player and I'm grateful him and his staff have shown that's what I need to do."

For the 80 minutes before those two goals in two minutes there was not a great deal to write home about.

The fizzing atmosphere Challinor was looking forward to after only tasting Hillsborough-lite in the EFL Trophy was flat for an hour because Wednesday's football was.

Although they were fortunate Roman Curtis' chest high tackle on Jamal Lowe only got a yellow card, Plymouth should have gone in at half-time multiple goals up.

Instead, when Bernard's goalbound header was nodded over at the end of the first half, Billy Mitchell’s deflected shot from the corner brought his first goal since 2021.

The second half was more even but Hillsborough helped its team over the line.

Having missed an easy chance from a quick throw-in, Keillor-Dunn poked home the loose ball at a badly-defended free-kick and at 2-0 the contest was over.

But the mouth-watering bit was still to come.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Mitchell, Heskey; Slattery, Bannan (Barry 72), J Lowe (Palmer 85); Keillor-Dunn (Gray 85).

Unused substitutes: Santos, Trueman, Weaver, Thornton.

Plymouth Argyle: Cooper; Harding, MacKenzie (Irow 63), Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White (Oseni 77), Ross; Amaechi, Ibrahim (Watts 63); Evans.

Unused substitutes: Storer, Campbell, Mwaro, Maund.

​The misses: Plymouth spurned some great chances, Xavier Amaechi horribly failing to make contact with a ball in from Bradley Ibrahim, then heading a great second-half chance from a Alex Hartridge cross wide. Earlier, Will Evans cushioned a volley into the side netting when Joe Lumley’s flapping at a corner left the goal gaping.

Star performers: Di’Shon Bernard was excellent but so too was midfielder Billy Mitchell, the stand-out Owls player in a first half where they were well below par.

Run over: This was the first time in eight league games Hillsborough’s attendance had officially fallen below 30,000 – though only by 772. The football did not lift them in the first half but they took it upon themselves to inspire the players around the hour.

#1878. Sheffield Wednesday's Dave Challinor on his summer set-piece education at Brentford

During his time out of work at the start of this season, Challinor visited the training grounds of Celtic, West Bromwich Albion and Brentford amongst others to broaden his horizons.

And the effect of his trip to see the Bees was evident on Saturday as the Owls registered their first win under him courtesy of two goals from set pieces to beat Plymouth Argyle.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Billy Mitchell opened the scoring with a shot which took a massive deflection at a 45th-minute corner. It was the midfielder's first goal since 2021.

Davis Keillor-Dunn then scored his sixth goal in nine matches when the Pilgrims failed to deal with a Callum Slattery free-kick.

Centre-back Di'Shon Bernard completed the scoring with a brilliant individual effort.

"I went to Brentford in the summer for a few days and saw how seriously they take it," said Challinor of set-pieces.

"They have set-pieces as part of every single training session for them, whether it's warm-ups or practise, delivery, finishing will be important. It's something that we are really keen to make sure we do practise and we do work at.

"It's not the most exciting thing in the world is it, practising set-piece delivery, but if you get the reinforcement on a Saturday it makes it a whole lot easier.

"We are really conscious and want to make sure the record we have is a positive one and Saturday helps.

"Keith (Andrews, Brentford's coach) was really helpful in me going up there so I spent a few days with them.

"It's an amazing environment, I learnt so much. There will be things from there that we'd love to incorporate here.

"It's a brilliantly run football club that have the success based on consistency right from the very top."

Wednesday's win, their first in seven matches in all competitions, took them above Tom Cleverley's Plymouth and back into the League One play-off places.

The result, it must be said, was better than the performance, and Challinor was not getting carried away at the end of his first league game as Owls manager, after consecutive cup defeats to begin his reign.

"I think we've got loads to do,” he said. “(At half-time) I was really open with the players and asked them what they thought. Sometimes it takes 10 minutes to earn the right (to play), sometimes it takes 60 minutes, sometimes you never earn the right.

"Plymouth are really good at asking questions of you, and in the first half I don't think we dealt with them questions well enough at times.

"We maybe needed to compete better and win first contacts and drop on second balls and track runners. We probably got away with it a little bit at times.

"But they were really honest about that and said that was the case.

"The second half was much, much better. I thought we dealt with their threats and then we were able to make the game look a little bit more like we'd want it to look like."

#1877. Spain vs England LIVE: Nations League result, latest updates and reaction

England defeated Spain 3-2 in a rollercoaster encounter to top their Nations League group. The Three Lions started in blistering fashion, going ahead through Harry Kane’s penalty in the first half, after the Ballon d’Or winner was felled by Pau Cubarsi.

It was two in the second period as Ezri Konsa nodded home from a Declan Rice corner, and Ben White slotted home a third as Thomas Tuchel’s men ran riot in Madrid. The tables turned when Elliot Anderson was sent off for a foul on Lamine Yamal, denying the Barcelona winger a clear goalscoring opportunity. Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting penalty, and the comeback was on.

Substitute Nico Williams notched a second as the world champions threatened a grandstand finish following Anthony Gordon’s mistake, as he was robbed in midfield by Pedri, who was the catalyst for change in the Spanish engine room after his half-time introduction. But it was England who held out, topping Group A3 to move into the knockout stages of this competition next year.

Thanks for joining us on Standard Sport, be sure to come back very soon for even more live action.

89 mins: Time is ticking away... can England hold on?

74 mins: Good save! Bellingham misses the ball at the far post and Oyarzabal brings it down. It falls for Fermin who strikes, but Trafford denies him.

#1876. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

There's loads of them now. Red and white shirts keep appearing in the home section behind the goal. https://t.co/3AonIYHKrL

Ipswich's first act of this game was to launch a long ball towards Marli Salmon and Zian Flemming. Salmon won the header, and then continued to win the overall battle with Flemming. Such an impressive performance by the 17yo. You don't see many defenders doing that at this age.

A post-match message to the support from Noni 🤳 pic.twitter.com/Eh6ojSkIfb

Full-time from a dramatic round of action in the Carabao Cup! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/YhtiwbB3Wn

Gyokeres ended up making 18 touches across the 90 minutes.

The Swede is not the type of player to take scores of touches (his average in the league last year was 18.14, so today was about on par for him), but you feel that there were opportunities for him to work into the half-spaces a bit more, as he did towards the end of the match.

Arteta’s side are through to the fourth round of the League Cup.

Plenty of talking points: Dowman, Salmon and an ominous Arsenal showing... Leave your thoughts on the match and join the conversation in the comments section beneath this live blog.

Ipswich Town 2 Arsenal 4 (Akpom) Davis picks out Akpom who swivels to deceive Konsa before sweeping home. There was perhaps a foul in the build-up as Lewis-Skelly appeared to get held back by the goalscorer as he scrambled to get back.

There will be two minutes of time added on.

Dowman seemingly makes history with every touch of the ball. A remarkable talent.

16 - The three youngest players to score in the League Cup for a Premier League side all did so for Arsenal:16y 212d - Cesc Fàbregas (vs Wolves, 2003)16y 258d - Max Dowman (vs Ipswich, 2026)16y 266d - Jack Wilshere (vs Sheffield United, 2008)Production. pic.twitter.com/cKPqcFUrpP

16 - Max Dowman is just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side in all competitions, after Wayne Rooney in October 2002 for Everton against Wrexham, also in the League Cup.Generations. pic.twitter.com/75XN6hgGeS

Arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.

And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.

Gyokeres finally gets a sniff at goal but Greaves is wise to his movement in behind and times a slide-tackle perfectly to poke the ball off for a corner.

A really assured performance from Salmon, who has completed all 61 one of his passes and marshalled Flemming and Akpom with maturity beyond his years.

Tzolis, who is booed by the home fans owing to his Norwich connections, has a glimpse at goal but is immediately closed down before Ipswich earn a corner after a swift transition but it is easily dealt with.

Arteta shuffles the pack again, taking off Eze and Madueke for Tzolis and Odegaard.

Florentino tries his luck from the edge of the box, but his effort is comfortably saved by Kepa despite taking a slight deflection off Konsa’s Achilles.

Another couple of substitutions for O’Neil, who will now be thinking about Everton next weekend. Davis and Walle Egeli are on for Ouattara and McAteer.

For those who are into your statistics, another Dowman goal here would create some history...

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 4 (Merino) Arsenal work the ball infield from the right in instalments, Madueke feeding Zubimendi who passes through Dowman to Merino on the edge of the box who opens up his body before guiding the ball around Walton.

Arsenal’s kick-off routines caused a stir last season, but this term they have mixed things up once more. Here, Zubimendi lays off Lewis-Skelly, who punches in a line-breaking pass to get Arsenal on the front foot from the off.

Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.

Arteta’s nine changes are looking fairly sensible now. He will be particularly pleased to have seen fringe players like Dowman and Madueke get on the scoresheet so emphatically. Arsenal will need their full squad to achieve their lofty goals this season and that half will give Arteta confidence that they have enough firepower to last the course.

We’ll play one minute of time added on...

Arsenal inject a bit of calm to proceedings with a healthy spell of possession. Their horizontal and vertical rotations (Lewis-Skelly is now minding to drop into that Rice role alongside the centre-backs) are proving tricky for Ipswich to track.

Gyokeres gets a shot away after a clever run in behind by Merino but cannot get enough pace behind his strike to trouble Walton.

Mehmeti brings down a searching ball from deep and faces up to Gabriel as he enters Arsenal box. Such is the Brazilian’s poise, though, that even when the Ipswich forward appears to have worked a yard of space, he telescopes in his leg and stops Mehmeti’s advances with perfunctory ease.

Ipswich are getting more bodies forward, with both full-backs bombing on. The ball is worked out to Furlong out on the right but, in a promising position, he loses his footing and the ball rolls out of play.

Next comes a foray down the left, Philogene beats Salmon on the outside but Kepa gets down smartly to cut out his cross. The next goal will naturally go a long way to determining how this tie plays out.

Ipswich are in the ascendancy and Greaves heads goalwards off a corner but does not get the requisite contact to beat Kepa. Arsenal launch a swift counter which is snuffed out by McAteer, illegally, and he goes into the book.

Ipswich might have thrown the towel in at 2-0 but they are pushing quite hard here and have caused Arsenal a few problems since the second goal. Philogene looks particularly dangerous on the left flank.

Outtara has been Ipswich’s best attacking outlet and he threads another lovely ball into the path of Philogene who is just beaten to it by Gabriel. The subsequent corner is punched away by Kepa.

Kepa goes long and Greaves misjudges the flight of the ball. Madueke looks to be in, but Ipswich’s centre-half recovers well and is able to block the eventual effort.

Merino picks out Dowman between the lines and the teenager is straight into Ipswich’s backline. His effort is well-struck but is charged down and cleared to safety.

Better from Ipswich! Their best shot at getting back into this contest is through counters when Arsenal are not set, and here Outtara bursts down the left before swinging in a deep cross to Flemming who cuts the ball back to Mehmeti who fires the ball just over the crossbar.

Guimaraes is slotting in between Arsenal’s split centre-backs in Arsenal’s build-up and Ipswich are not prepared to go three vs three that high up the pitch meaning the Brazilian has all the time in the world to dictate play from there. We’ve seen this all season long from Rice.

Arsenal are in complete control. Madueke flashes a delivery across the face of goal which is just cut out by Kipre before Gyokeres can get a foot in.

Arsenal’s midfield is so powerful and they showed it there, as Guimaraes slammed into one tackle and then Merino followed up with another to create the chance for Madueke. Arsenal are completely dominant here.

A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2 (Madueke) That is goal of Ipswich’s own making. Walton’s loose pass out is picked off by livewire Guimaraes, and Merino spins in a ball in behind for Madueke to stride on to and spear beyond Walton into the bottom corner.

Arsenal are flying 🔥Noni Madueke adds a second for the Gunners 🔴 pic.twitter.com/gAVmAI3odx

Florentino’s loose pass is picked off by Dowman and the youngster earns a free-kick as the Ipswich midfielder attempts to recover. It’s taken quickly and Eze bursts into the box - there is a half-hearted shout for a penalty as the ball appears to strike Ouattara’s arm but the contact appears incidental and the referee waves play on.

Max Dowman’s second goal for Arsenal is quite similar to his first, scored so thrillingly against Everton last season. On both occasions he has put an opposition defender face-first in the turf before scoring the goal. Outrageous ability with the ball at his feet.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

Ipswich earn a free-kick on the left by-line but Gyokeres does his job at the near post and heads away Nunez’s delivery.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1 (Dowman) Simply majestic. A simple one-two with Eze on the left has Dowman running at Ipswich’s defence. He drops his shoulder and sells Kipre a dream before stroking the ball beyond Walton. “1-0 to the champions” sing the travelling fans.

Lewis-Skelly bursts down the left and picks out Dowman on the edge of the box. He attempts to tee up Guimaraes but Nunez gets a toe in and is able to avert the danger.

Early indications suggest Zubimendi will play in the nominal right-back position, inverting into midfield when Arsenal build up.

Madueke picks up the ball on the right flank and drifts inside before Guimaraes’ effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Flemming gets us started. Ipswich kicking from right to left.

The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts. Last week Arsenal were made to change into red shorts to avoid a similar clash with Napoli, but apparently that’s no problem tonight. Modern football for ya!

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1875. Tuttosport: Milan rekindle interest in Bologna star amid feeling of regret

AC Milan still retain an interest in signing Juan Miranda after being linked with him in previous years, a report claims.

Tuttosport write this morning that Miranda is establishing himself as one of the best specialists in his position in Europe. The numbers speak for themselves: he’s already provided six assists in the first part of the season.

No one in Serie A has more than that, and his creativity was seen first hand in Bologna’s comeback win at San Siro. Naturally, his performances have not gone unnoticed in Italy and England. The first inquiries are beginning to arrive, with a contract situation that is worth keeping an eye on.

The paper writes that Miranda is also appreciated by Milan, although the Rossoneri are kicking themselves a bit too. They had an agreement to sign him on a free transfer two years ago and then decided to walk away. In hindsight, it looks like a big mistake.

Bologna seized the transfer opportunity in the summer of 2024, and are now enjoying his exploits. At the same time, however, concern is beginning to mount given that his deal with the Rossoblu expires in just 19 months.

This is why the Bologna management have been trying to establish talks regarding a contract extension in the past few weeks. The work so far hasn’t led to great progress, and so the possibility of a sale to avoid losing the Spaniard in a cut-price deal (or even for free) may be evaluated.

Juventus are in the running too, and an immediate attempt to bring him to Continassa and give Luciano Spalletti the left-back he’s coveted since last summer can’t be ruled out. This is especially true if the Bianconeri are in contention for a top-four finish.

Beware of the Palladino effect: since the coach took over at Bologna, the Rossoblu have been soaring (17 points in seven games). If the Emilian side were to also be involved in the fight for a European spot, it would be more difficult to pry Miranda from them.

#1873. Spain 2-3 England: Thomas Tuchel’s ten men hold on for famous, group-topping victory

England ended 2026 with an extraordinary 3-2 triumph in world champions Spain’s backyard as Thomas Tuchel’s 10 men dug deep to top their Nations League group on a magical night in Madrid.

An intense year that included a heartbreaking World Cup semi-final collapse to Argentina and wild bronze-medal win against France concluded with a chaotic victory against adversity akin to the unforgettable last-16 triumph in Mexico.

England roared into an unthinkable three-goal lead at the Metropolitano, where Harry Kane’s penalty gave the visitors a deserved half-time lead that they quickly added to as Ezri Konsa and Ben White silenced Spain.

But Elliot Anderson’s sending off in the 63rd minute for bringing down Lamine Yamal after Jarell Quansah was caught out put them on the backfoot against the World Cup winners.

Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting spot-kick and fellow Euro 2024 final goalscorer Nico Williams came off the bench to reduce the deficit as Tuchel’s team attempted to batten down the hatches.

England were made to sweat and James Trafford, given the nod in goal ahead of Jordan Pickford, produced some vital saves to help bring Spain’s 43-game unbeaten record to an end.

Wild celebrations greeted the final whistle, with the statement win seeing Tuchel’s side through to the Nations League quarter-finals as Group A3 winners.

#1872. Jude Bellingham says he 'wants to be a gentleman' but admits he doesn't feel 'mature' because 'I can't cook, I can't drive and I rely on my family' in new smouldering photoshoot

Published: 10:54 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 13:36 EST, 10 November 2026

Real Madrid and England star Jude Bellingham has admitted he doesn't feel 'mature', despite being labelled as such from a young age.

The midfielder, 23, has impressed with his level head and assured public speaking since breaking onto the professional scene at 16 and living under the glare of the public eye in his formative years.

But Bellingham has confessed that his complete attention to detail as a footballer has left deficiencies in other areas of his life, such as cooking or driving.

Speaking to Vogue in an interview accompanying a fashion photoshoot in which he's dressed to fit the 60s and 70s aesthetic he leans into, Bellingham also spoke about his desire to be a role model for the younger generation.

'I feel mature in a football context because I’ve played nearly 400 games, but in a life context I don’t feel that mature now, to be honest,' he told Vogue.

'I can’t cook, I can’t drive… I’m good at what I do, but everything else? Not that great. I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else.

Jude Bellingham poses for Vogue during a photoshoot displaying his love of 60s fashion

Bellingham admits he isn't mature in some areas of his life - seen here holding up his provisional driving licence

'That’s where I’m at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I’ve probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there’ll be a time and a place for that, I’m sure.'

Bellingham plays with a fierce competitive spirit on the pitch but is aware of his responsibility to behave away from football, adding: 'I’ve always said that, off the pitch, I want to be a gentleman.'

The Real superstar, who is in a relationship with American influencer and model Ashlyn Castro, went on: 'You can’t just behave how you want but then still represent a city or a country every time you wear their shirt, because you are inspiring [someone].

'Whether you like it or not, you are looked up to by the next generation. I prefer to see it as a privilege.'

The photoshoot for the fashion magazine showcased Bellingham's sense of style, which he says is rooted in his admiration for iconic characters from the 60s and 70s such as Elvis Presley, Michael Caine and James Bond movies of the era.

The Vogue cover shows Bellingham in a dark brown suit and coat with wide lapels and a bright orange cardigan, while he appears in a herringbone overcoat and white chino shorts in another.

Another image shows Bellingham holding up his green provisional driving licence.

Bellingham, selected in the England squad for upcoming internationals against Croatia and Spain, is in a rich vein of form.

Bellingham is pictured in a sharp suit and says he is inspired by iconic figures of yesteryear

The cover star feels a responsibility to be a gentleman and positive role model

Under Jose Mourinho's management at the Bernabeu this season, he's scored four goals and provided four assists already in LaLiga, with the Spanish giants three points behind Barcelona in the title race.

He's joined in the England squad by his younger brother, Jobe, and is flying high for the national side now his relationship with Tuchel is on an even keel.

Last Friday, the Three Lions manager said: 'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

On Jobe being called up from the Under-21s, he added: 'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

Bellingham poses in more casual attire, pairing a vintage Adidas sweater with pin stripe trousers

'I think he actually watched training very early in my reign. He came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and said it would be nice if one day he was with him.

'He was very kind and very polite and I'm glad to have him in camp. Everyone will compare them and he has to live with this.

'They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. Jobe is more defensive. I think they are also different characters, at least that's what I heard.

'He couldn't stop smiling when I called to tell him the news. He has the same beautiful smile like Jude so it's nice to have him.'

#1871. How Harrogate Town banished ghosts of Carlisle United with 4-0 rout of Altrincham - analysis

When Altrincham defender Reuben Lopata-White lunged in on Harrogate Town winger Ellis Taylor, there will have been two shivers down the spines of the home supporters.

The first one being the natural one, brought on by the reckless nature of the loaned-out Leeds United prospect’s foul. The second will have been prompted by the dawning realisation of what comes next.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Harrogate have not had the best of times against 10-man sides and lost 3-0 to a Carlisle United side who saw two men sent off less than three weeks ago.

Halloween has been and gone, but the ghosts of Carlisle threatened to haunt when the red card was brandished on the 13-minute mark.

“I think everyone in the stadium thought that [it was going to be a struggle],” said Harrogate boss Simon Weaver. “[Altrincham] probably, ultimately, were buoyed by the fact that it didn't go our way the last time.

“It's not a case of sulking and berating everyone when it just didn't work on that occasion, but are we capable of next time, especially against a really good team like Altrincham, carrying out our roles a bit better?”

To say Harrogate carried out their roles a bit better would be an understatement. The strong Sulphurite grip on the game rarely loosened as they cruised to an emphatic 4-0 win.

It took until the second half but once the hosts started firing on all cylinders in the final third, the afternoon raced away from the Robins.

Will McGowan drew first blood shortly after the restart and Morgan Williams pounced merely 10 minutes later.

Pressure continued to be applied and the advantage was built upon by Michael Craig and Rohan Vaughan, who both hammered home thunderous strikes.

Ellis Taylor may not have etched his name on the scoresheet but the Marcy Fitness Stadium became his playground, one in which he toyed with defenders with relative ease.

“We still had to be very patient,” said Weaver. “[We had] to really break through and put the game to bed.

“We did in the end and that's what mattered and a growing maturity I thought the lads showed today.

“You’ve got to kill off the hope, kill off the energy and psychologically I think the best way of doing it is to keep the ball and keep probing and not get flustered ourselves.”

Boreham Wood have steamed away at the top of the National League table but it remains early days. Harrogate reduced the gap between the sides to 10 points and will be keen to keep chipping away.

As for the ghosts of Carlisle - consider them banished.

“I think we've got a really good, honest group,” said Weaver. “There’s blips on the journey of every team but 18 new players and people are handling disappointments well, people aren't getting over the top or egotistical when we bang a few goals in.

“They want to play and they want to play in the right way but not play boring football. We’ve got a proud record at home.”

#1869. Declan Rice reveals bold England prediction that came true in stunning Spain victory

Declan Rice has claimed England “knew” they would beat world champions Spain.

The Three Lions finished top of their Nations League group ahead of the Spanish on Sunday with a stunning 3-2 win over the world champions.

After goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White put the visitors three goals up, Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts made their way back to within one. But England held on for victory to overtake their hosts in the group.

Following the game, the Arsenal midfielder spoke about the confidence his side will take from their victory and claimed Thomas Tuchel’s team knew they were going to claim all three points in Madrid.

“We knew we were going to beat them tonight,” Rice told ITV.

“The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive. The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played. Pressure, pressure. Overall, 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against a team unbeaten in 43 [matches] is massive.”

Rice added: “Argentina that day [in the World Cup semi-finals] wasn’t meant to be. That’s football.

“When they [Spain] got a second [goal], maybe it could have gone another way. It’s a massive win. Everything happened so quickly [at the end], so for him [James Trafford] to make two in the space of two seconds is massive.”

England, as group winners, will have a favourable draw for the quarter-finals of the Nations League, and they will find out their opponents on Friday.

They will face a runner-up from one of the other three ‘Group A’ tables.

Thomas Tuchel saluted Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford following his stellar display in England’s 3-2 Nations League win over Spain.

The Three Lions raced into a three-goal lead in Madrid last night (November 15) as Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White weighed in with goals.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Elliot Anderson’s red card buoyed Spain, who hit back through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but a comeback could not be completed.

England boss Tuchel gave Trafford the spot between the sticks and the 24-year-old vindicated the decision, making some excellent stops. He made a particularly impressive double save in stoppage time, denying Fermin Lopez and then keeping Oyarzabal’s follow-up out.

Tuchel said: “Very good. That's his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions.

"We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments. The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.

Trafford’s competitor for the England gloves is Everton’s Jordan Pickford, who has spent the bulk of the last decade as the first-choice stopper.

Across the last two international breaks, playing time has been split evenly between the pair.

Last week, Trafford’s Leeds teammate and Pickford’s former Everton teammate Dominic Calvert-Lewin said: “I think we're fortunate now that we've got two exceptional goalkeepers. One thing that is true for both of them is they're very self-confident and confident in their ability, which is what I think you need from England's number one.

“I played with Pickers for nine years at Everton, so I've seen him grow and what a career he's had for England. I don't think that can be so quickly disregarded at all.

“But now I'm playing with James Trafford, who is a younger, confident, top, top goalkeeper, and I'm seeing his quality week in, week out now. I think it's something that should be appreciated by us as a nation.”

#1865. How Thomas Tuchel instilled winning England instinct to secure historic victory over Spain

When Thomas Tuchel and his England coaching staff come to reflect on England’s sensational victory in Spain, they will come to the conclusion it could scarcely have gone better.

Such a statement may feel bizarre given the visitors were at one stage 3-0 up with cruise control applied, before another Jarell Quansah error led to an Elliot Anderson red card, a penalty converted, and then a second goal back for a Spain team totally rejuvenated.

The reality, though, is that if England’s canter to a one-sided victory had continued as it was doing, Tuchel and his team would have far less to pore over as they unpick the headers and volleys at the end of this calendar year and the learning they can take from what still finished - by getting over the line 3-2 and topping the group - a hugely successful international break.

Tuchel had repeatedly described this affair as “a final” in the days leading up, but just as important as finishing top of the group and the potentially easier quarter-final opponent it could secure them in March was delivering a performance to provide encouragement that the Three Lions can indeed go toe-to-toe with the very best and avoid unforced errors in the process.

OK, there was one such mistake: Quansah, at fault for Croatia’s goal at Wembley on Thursday, dawdling on the ball and conceding possession cheaply. England’s magnificent earlier work threatened to unravel at that point as the dominoes of the resultant red card, goal and second strike fell.

But then came the memories of the cavalry this summer, their resolute World Cup closing-it-out jobs against Mexico and then Norway and then the ugly attempt to do it all over again at the semi-final against Argentina. Instinct kicked in.

James Trafford getting the nod ahead of Jordan Pickford in the Spanish capital was a bold call, as was Ben White starting at right-back and Lewis Hall on the left, but all three were superb, as the head coach’s big decisions were wholly vindicated. The world champions’ unbeaten run was ended by England, the Spanish tasting defeat in Madrid for the first time in 39 years, since a certain Gary Lineker netted all four in a 4-2 England win.

Lamine Yamal posed England all sorts of questions from the right wing - a fabulous player - but did he cause them a wealth of problems? Aside from a simple assist for Spain’s second, no, not really. Hall was sturdy at left-back, just as England were all over the pitch.

Their first-half display, after which point they led 1-0 through a Harry Kane penalty, was described by Roy Keane in ITV’s coverage as “perfect”. They had certainly all been on the same wavelength, their passing sequences all crisp. And in the second half, after those two quickfire goals shipped, the defensive equivalent of that joined-up thinking was visible from a team that looked like one.

The players involved in this Nations League group game represent many of the Champions League powerhouses and yet there was no hint of this being an unwanted match that disrupts the club football juggernaut and where there is a needless risk of injury. Not a bit of that. When Jude Bellingham’s number came up and he was substituted in the 83rd minute, presumably to keep Real Madrid happy, he looked angered not to be carrying on in a game that had just about everything. What’s more: it had the result that England craved. And expected.

“We knew we were going to beat them tonight,” said Declan Rice. Not only a thrilling night for England, it will also have taught them plenty about themselves. That is just as important.
