#1863. Spurs finally score... but still lose

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”

Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc

🗣️ "The young players give us energy" 💪Andoni Iraola is very pleased with the way the Liverpool youngsters played after beating Spurs 3-1 at Anfield 👏#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup | @markpougatch | @Robbie9Fowler pic.twitter.com/bHjOrmccH2

🗣️"Szoboszlai scores A LOT OF BANGERS"😂Needless to say Cody Gakpo was really impressed with Dominik Szoboszlai's goal for Liverpool 👏#ITVFootball | @LFC | @Carabao_Cup | @gabrielclarke05 pic.twitter.com/O3bs6Y9M2p

"They've done themselves proud!" 👏Conor Coady on Lewis Koumas performance for Liverpool 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3JGkuY7Eye

Moments after the ball thumped into the back of the net:

Possession: Liverpool 44%-56% TottenhamShots: 12-17Shots on target: 5-6Corners: 5-9Touches in opposition box: 22-27

Andrew Robertson received a great reception from the Anfield crowd whilst warming up, when he came on and now at full-time. He catches up with old teammates as he heads off in the pouring rain, applauding the Liverpool fans.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool book their place in the fourth round of the League Cup courtesy of a 3-1 win over Tottenham. Andoni Iraola’s side scored three stunning goals to seal their progression.

Mamardashvili does well to save from a deflection, like he did a few minutes ago. Mamardashvili did not cover himself in glory for Tottenham’s goal but has made some great saves tonight.

Oh my word! The Hungarian loves a screamer and this is another to add to the list. It is similar to a goal Suarez scored at The Kop End against Norwich a number of years ago. Szoboszlai chests it down and from nearly 30 yards out smashes across the ball. The ball flies into to the top corner, always going away from Dubravka, and Szoboszlai celebrates in front of The Kop. A quite incredible goal.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

There will be four added minutes at Anfield.

Savio has an effort from the right side of the box but drags his shot wide of the far post.

Liverpool counter with Mamardashvili’s long ball forward for Isak, who gets the better of Gray on the left side of the box. Isak gets his shot away and the ball appeared to hit Tosin’s arm but the penalty is not given. Replays show it did hit Tosin’s arm and he is lucky there is not VAR tonight as that could well have been overturned.

Solanke is on for Tottenham in place of Tel as the visitors have a corner out on the right. Tottenham take it short before the delivery is swung in and headed away by Gakpo as the rain comes thrashing down again at Anfield.

Tottenham keep it alive and Marmoush has an effort from the left side of the box. It deflects off Araujo and Mamardashvili makes a stunning save.

Szoboszlai should bury a guilt-edge chance inside the Tottenham penalty area but his effort is saved. There was a suspicion of offside against Szoboszlai but the flag did not go up. Szoboszlai was being played onside by quite some way by Gray so a huge missed opportunity.

That is superb one-vs-one defending from Jacquet. The ball is played down the left channel but Jacquet gets the better of Marmoush.

Into the final 10 minutes we go at Anfield.

Liverpool are under pressure at the moment as Tottenham attack the Anfield Road End, where the travelling Spurs supporters are housed. Mamardashvili is again unconvincing when dealing with a corner into the box.

Double change for Tottenham as Savio and Maddison replace Kudus and Gallagher.

That is a stupid challenge from Kerkez, who is booked for a silly foul on Gallagher. Kerkez was asking for a booking for that challenge and referee Andy Madley obliges.

Change for Liverpool as Barcola replaces Ngumoha.

The visitors take advantage of very poor keeping from Mamardashvili. Fernandes’ delivery should be dealt with by Mamardashvili but the Georgian keeper flaps at empty air. It comes to Gallagher, who has a simple header from just a few yards out. A lifeline for Tottenham, who have their first goal this season against Premier League opposition.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

Tottenham have had some decent chances tonight. The latest comes for Gallagher just inside the Liverpool box but his effort takes a deflection off Kerkez and goes behind for a corner...

That is a crucial challenge from Kerkez inside his own box. Marmoush looked like he was going to have a great opportunity from 10 yards out in the centre of Liverpool’s penalty area but Kerkez intervenes with a superbly-timed challenge to deny the Egyptian.

Double change for Liverpool as Szoboszlai and Gravenberch replace Nyoni and McConnell in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield.

Mamardashvili makes an important save. Marmoush carries the ball a long way down Tottenham’s left before cutting inside. As he gets to the Liverpool box, he plays the ball across to his right to find Kudus, whose first-time effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his left.

Robertson is going to come on for Tottenham against his former side and receives a great reception from the Liverpool fans, similarly to the reception Ray Clemence received all those years ago:

Tosin decides to shoot from range but drags his effort wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

The home side double their lead at The Kop end. Kerkez perhaps should shoot from the edge of the box but instead lays it back to Mac Allister. The Argentine then plays it to his left to find Gakpo, who cuts inside onto his right and fires into the far corner. This now his tenth goal in 13 League Cup appearances.

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

No chances to speak of in the early stages of this second half.

We are back under way at Anfield. Liverpool have made a change at the break with Jacquet coming on for Gomez. This was Gomez’s first game back after injury.

Tottenham did have two big chances through Bergvall and Kudus and there are arguments to say both of them should have scored.

Mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

We are past the two initial minutes added on but that is because of the delay when Senesi was given a talking-to moments ago. That allows Liverpool to win a free-kick not far outside the Tottenham box and Bentancur is booked for the foul on Gakpo.

This will be the final moment of the half.

Senesi absolutely clatters into McConnell but somehow escapes without a booking. There have been a number of soft yellows in this first yet one of the most blatant yellows is not given as a booking.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Marmoush is the first Tottenham player booked tonight for a foul on McConnell and that feels on the harsh side. Definitely a foul but was it a yellow?

That is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

Mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. McConnell then feeds a pass into the box to pick out the run of Koumas, who squares it for Mac Allister. The Argentine cannot get his feet sorted in time and wastes the opportunity from eight yards out.

Liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. It was a clumsy challenge from Senesi and if VAR was in action tonight it would have been interesting to see what they would have done with that as Senesi did barge into the back of McConnell.

Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

There is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

That is a big chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

What a goal......that would of been! 🫢Kudus fires over what would of been a sensational move from Spurs#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup pic.twitter.com/a1TPzKyJlP

Gomez gives the ball away cheaply inside his own half before McConnell is penalised for a foul on Marmoush. Will Tottenham cross it or take the shot on from around 25 yards out? The answer is the latter and Marmoush goes for goal but misses the target.

That was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

The way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a new contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

He scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

Koumas takes a great first touch before getting his shot away but is denied by Dubravka. Both goalkeepers have now been forced into good saves early doors.

Close for Lewis Koumas!The Liverpool youngster is denied by Martin Dubravka after some brilliant play by Rio Ngumoha 🪄 pic.twitter.com/YNC8QEAGGG

Tottenham are dominating possession thus far, with a lot of the game being played in Liverpool’s half at the moment.

The heavens have well and truly opened at Anfield, with the rain heaving down.

Tottenham win a corner off Gomez out on the right. Kudus clips in an inswinger that Araujo heads away.

Gakpo is starting out on the left for Liverpool tonight, with Ngumoha on the right and Koumas leading the line down the centre. Gakpo was linked with a move to Tottenham and Manchester City over the summer but stayed at Liverpool.

Tottenham have a free-kick not far outside the Liverpool penalty area on the right as Kerkez is penalised for blocking Gallagher’s cross with his arm. Kudus’ delivery is headed away by Araujo.

Kudus keeps it alive and sends in another cross that ends up in Mamardashvili’s arms.

We are under way at Anfield, with a place in the fourth round at stake.

Djaksparo is a rising musician from Paris who who gained viral fame following a social media boost from Liverpool’s summer signing Bradley Barcola, who is on the bench for the hosts this evening.

During the Spaniard’s three seasons at the helm at Bournemouth, he never made it past the fourth round in this competition. He reached the fourth round in his first season at Bournemouth during the 2023/24 season but in the last two seasons has fallen in the second round, which was the round Bournemouth entered the competition.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Zubimendi’s injury will come as a blow for the Gunners, despite the Spaniard struggling for game time at the Emirates Stadium after the summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes and the form of Declan Rice, who starred for his country once more on Sunday evening.

#1861. GdS: Club Brugge name price for Tresoldi – why a difficult negotiation beckons for Milan

AC Milan have already discovered the starting price for Nicolo Tresoldi, and it’s safe to say it will not be a cheap deal.

According to this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), it is no secret that Tresoldi sits at the top of the wish list for Milan. Gerry Cardinale, first and foremost, is a big admirer of the rising Brugge star.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is equally well-known that the striker has been a lifelong fan of the Rossoneri. However, his contract runs until 2029, so to take him away from the Jan Breydel Stadium a negotiation is needed with a club that are tough to deal with, as the past shows.

The phone lines between Milan and Brugge were first used in 2022, when the Charles De Ketelaere saga took place. Since then, the management teams at both Milan and the Belgian club have changed, but the history between the two sides should help facilitate discussions. Ardon Jashari was another arduous negotiation, but one that eventually reached the finish line too.

In the cases of De Ketelaere and Jashari, the pitch has arguably favoured the seller more than the buyer. Perhaps the outcome will be different with Tresoldi, should the two parties actually sit down to negotiate.

One caveat: especially in January, the asking is bound to be significant. How significant? Around €60m, according to whispers from Flanders.

Club Brugge are accustomed to selling their best players when the time comes, but they are under no pressure to do so, especially while the season is still underway. Tresoldi has effectively carried the team on his back, scoring eight goals in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Super Cup.

The total: 14 goals in 17 official matches. For the club to part ways with their star striker during the mid-season window – a time when all their competitive objectives remain within reach – the offer would certainly need to be more than substantial.

Furthermore, if the 22-year-old forward maintains his current scoring rate throughout the season, his market value will only continue to climb. It is a risk, but also an opportunity. Moreover, Milan are not alone in the race for Tresoldi.

Bayern Munich and top English clubs are keeping a close eye on the former Hannover man, who was born in Cagliari but is a key player for the German U21 national team. Consequently, if Cardinale wishes to beat the competition, he would need to act quickly and decisively.

🎬 Nicolò Tresoldi 🔴⚫️ https://t.co/tDcsnRgXiM

— AngelRedblack- MX #MilanSpace ❤🔴⚫ (@Angelredblack1) November 11, 2026

He demonstrated he can dothis over the summer with the signings of Gonçalo Ramos, Diego Moreira, and Mario Gila. However, authorising a €60m expenditure would require the right conditions: specifically, Milan must be in the hunt for a major objective.

Tresoldi’s arrival could not see him then become a back-up to Gonçalo Ramos, the most expensive signing in the club’s history. In essence, it requires Ruben Amorim to provide the necessary assurances regarding the wisdom of the acquisition.

Meanwhile, Tresoldi’s hat-trick against Inter at San Siro on October 13th in the Champions League has naturally excited the Rossoneri fans, who would be more than happy to embrace him. However, they aren’t the ones who have to pay the €60m.

Leeds United icon Pablo Hernandez has conceded it was “difficult” to end his lengthy association with the Whites in 2021.

The 41-year-old is a beloved figure in LS11 having spent five years dazzling supporters with his trickery and eye for a killer pass.

He was a crucial figure in the club’s Championship title-winning 2019/20 campaign and later represented Leeds in the Premier League.

Now retired and the head coach of his hometown club Castellon in Spain’s second tier, former playmaker Hernandez has discussed his Leeds exit in an interview with the Daily Star.

He said: “It was difficult to leave Leeds. Maybe I could have played another year at Leeds.

“I don't know what would have happened if I'd stayed, but I think whenever I've made a decision in my career, I've always believed it was the right one.”

Hernandez ended his playing career back in his native Spain with Castellon, who he is now leading on a charge up the Segunda Division from the dugout. The club sit second, with only Almeria above them in the rankings.

Hernandez said: “I think everybody in England, and probably around the world, believes Leeds should be playing in the Premier League. For me, they're one of the best clubs in England.

“I feel the same way about Castellon. I think we have some of the best fans in Spain, and we deserve the opportunity to play in La Liga again and show that we're a big club.

“Leaving Castellon for Valencia [as a youngster] was a difficult decision. But at that time, the club didn't have the best owners or the best organisation, particularly within the academy. But I always had the feeling that one day I would come back to Castellon.”

#1859. From crying kid to Ballon d'Or hopeful: How fearless Rio Ngumoha toughened up, via quitting Chelsea for Liverpool at just 15 and being shielded from 'crime and stuff' in East London

Published: 14:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ngumoha is back in with the older boys, only this time there are no tears.

It is hard to believe the Liverpool and England winger could ever feel intimidated on a football pitch, given his talent was so apparent at the age of six that his older brother, James, gave up school to coach him.

Ngumoha can smile about the tears now, for sitting here at 18 years old as a full international on the verge of his first Three Lions start is a happy ending.

'I was six, maybe only five, playing for a local team,' he recalls, holding court with journalists at England's base of the Tottenham Hotspur training ground. 'I got an assist and I could hear my mum on the side saying, "Well done". Then I heard them saying that I was playing with older boys, and I just panicked. I started crying and walked off the pitch. I was so scared because everyone was older than me.'

Ngumoha is the youngest player in Thomas Tuchel's 26-man squad for this week's Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. Harry Kane is 15 years his senior.

'After that game, I realised I could have definitely competed with them,' he adds. 'So yeah, I've toughened up a bit.'

Rio Ngumoha is the youngest player in the England squad after years of 'toughening up'

Ngumoha quit Chelsea for Liverpool because he says: 'I felt like I needed a new challenge'

Tougher, wiser and, what becomes clear when talk turns to Kane's Ballon d'Or, is that Ngumoha has grown in confidence, too. So confident, in fact, that not only does he want one of his own, he believes the game's ultimate individual honour is not beyond his reach.

The question was put to him, admittedly, but he took it and ran with it, much like he does the football.

'Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or is a big, big thing,' says Ngumoha, in keeping with his generation's fascination with the prize. 'Being known as the best player in the world… I would like to achieve it, and I think I can do it.'

A misplaced belief after less than 20 senior starts? You would ordinarily argue so, but Ngumoha's talent appears so rare that it's better to imagine where it could go, not where it cannot. I was there in Tampa in the summer when, then 17, he played the second half of England's 1-0 World Cup warm-up win over New Zealand. Come the end, he had been the best winger on the pitch. We wondered then if there was still a way into the squad for a player only in the States to train at the Florida pre-camp.

'I knew before going to the camp that I couldn't go to the World Cup anyway,' - it turns out he was not on the provisional 55-man list - says Ngumoha. 'So I just chose the pre-camp to prove myself, to be free, to play with some expression. I did that and I made a good impression.'

He achieved that on his debut in Tampa by beating his man, and the man after that, too. I put it to him that dribbling is a lost art.

'I feel like I'm quite fearless,' he says, after nodding in agreement. 'If there's an opportunity to beat my man, I'll always do it. It was the way I grew up, really, playing in cages near my house. Even at Chelsea, sometimes, they just let me play free. Then when I moved to Liverpool, I've never really been told to stop. I like exciting people. I like getting people off their seat.'

Ngumoha shows a quiet maturity and has been starring in the Premier League for Liverpool

To recap, Ngumoha was raised in East London by his mother and brother. He reveals that, through football, they shielded him from 'crime and stuff'. Football was 'an escape route'. He played for Chelsea's academy from the age of eight but left at 15 to join Liverpool. Why?

'I felt like I needed a new challenge,' he says. 'Like if I had stayed at Chelsea... I'm not saying that I wouldn't have got to the first-team as quick, because I believe in my ability, but I feel like Liverpool just gave me a new pathway.

'The plan they set for me was straightforward. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool. They just said, if I prove myself, because they knew how much ability I had, they knew that I would definitely be a first-team player and a star-in-the-making for them. It has been the right choice so far.'

For one so young, there is quiet maturity to Ngumoha, one that means FA staff have permitted this interview. Often, the fledglings are kept closer to the nest. But then, there is a reminder of his youthful innocence.

'Nando's is still my fantasy meal,' he says. 'I get sweet potatoes, four boneless thighs, peri-tamer, some garlic bread. They need to give me a little sponsorship, the Nando's Black Card!'

The exclusive card he mentions gives the holder and up to four guests complimentary food for one year. The career that awaits Ngumoha means free chicken should be the least of his rewards. The boy who once cried when he discovered he was playing with the big boys believes that, one day, he can be the biggest of them all.

#1858. Thomas Tuchel reveals key reason why England beat Spain in ‘best performance’ of his tenure

Thomas Tuchel has explained why England’s 3-2 win over Spain was the best performance of his tenure.

The German has been in charge of the Three Lions since January 2025 and guided them to third place at the World Cup in the summer, their highest finish in the competition since their only title in 1966.

That included memorable wins against Croatia, DR Congo and Mexico. Last month, in the Nations League, England inflicted upon Croatia the heaviest defeat in their history as they thrashed Slaven Bilic’s side 7-0 in Rijeka.

But Tuchel admitted he views Sunday’s 10-man victory over the world champions in Madrid as the finest performance during his time at the helm.

Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored for the Three Lions as they ended the world champions’ 43-game unbeaten streak despite conceding twice in the second half. It secured England top spot in their Nations League group ahead of Spain.

“Brilliant performance,” Tuchel told ITV after the game. “A well deserved win. Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

“It was a complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit-wise, energy-wise and also football quality was highest level.

“We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.”

Speaking about how England dug in defensively once Spain had scored their second goal, Tuchel said: “Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]. That’s the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners.”

Asked what England showed, he replied: “What we are made of and what we can do. We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years [at the World Cup] and we weren’t happy with it. It’s impressive what we did in the last two camps.”

#1854. Ibrahimovic shares feelings on ‘bond’ with Milan: “The most important team in my life”

Zlatan Ibrahimovic has shed light on just how much AC Milan mean to him, labelling it the ‘most important’ club he has represented.

Today marks the launch of ‘Il Milan nel Mondo’, Mauro Suma’s new book exploring the Rossoneri’s reach beyond both Milan and Italy. Several Rossoneri Legends will join the author at the launch this morning, including Daniele Massaro, Demetrio Albertini and Filippo Galli.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ibrahimovic wrote a foreword in the book, which has been relayed by MilanNews. The RedBird Capital senior advisor spoke about just how much the club means to him, after his two spells as a player and now his time as an executive.

“Milan are the most important team in my life. And it’s also the only one that convinced me to return. In my career, I’ve worn legendary shirts, played in wonderful cities, and won everywhere. But Milan was something different,” he said.

“It was the only club that truly drew me back, the only one where I felt the need to start over. Convincing Zlatan to return isn’t easy. It’s not easy for anyone. Yet, with Milan, it’s happened more than once.

“This means that between me and these colours, a bond has been created that goes beyond football, beyond trophies, even beyond time. Victory remains in the halls of fame; some teams, however, stay with you. AC Milan belongs to this category.

“The first time, AC Milan brought me happiness, the second, love. In the Rossoneri, I found a sense of belonging that is increasingly rare in modern football. Because starting an adventure with a club can happen. Returning a second time, and then again, means that the club and its fans have become part of you.

“AC Milan are the most successful Italian club at international level, but it’s not just a collection of trophies. It’s an identity. It’s a way of being in football and in the world. Wherever it goes, it leaves a mark. And those who join AC Milan, sometimes, never leave.”

Ibrahimovic signed the first time in August 2010 after an experience at Barcelona that wasn’t a positive one, and he helped Milan to the Scudetto with a 14-goal haul. He won the Capocannoniere the next season, doubling that tally.

He returned in 2019 and scored 25 goals in 37 appearances in his first two campaigns, securing a return to European competitions. At the end of his third season, the climb was complete: the Rossoneri won their 19th league title.

Then, in June 2023 came his emotional farewell at San Siro, before Zlatan returned to the club but wearing a suit and tie.

#1851. Man United chiefs set for Monaco summit TOMORROW to decide Michael Carrick's fate... as Ineos face taking their compensation for sacked managers and executives over £30m

Published: 02:40 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 15:11 EST, 10 November 2026

Michael Carrick's fate as Manchester United head coach will be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

If United decide to sack Carrick, it would push the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the favourite to take over, and buying the Argentine out of his contract with the US national team would cost another £7million.

Berrada and Wilcox flew to the south of France on Tuesday to attend a scheduled summit of Ineos executives.

Berrada and Wilcox will make their recommendation to Ratcliffe on Wednesday, with all the indications pointing to Carrick paying the price for his team’s alarming descent into the Premier League relegation zone.

United sources are maintaining that no final decision has been reached. Co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer would still need to give their approval for the sacking.

Michael Carrick is pictured arriving at Manchester United's training ground at 7.15am

Mauricio Pochettino is the frontrunner to replace Carrick - leaving his role as US head coach

Who do you think is truly to blame for United¿s disastrous season - the manager or the club¿s leadership?

It’s understood that the Old Trafford hierarchy would want to inform Carrick of their decision face to face, so there may not be any official confirmation from the club until Thursday.

The 45-year-old turned up for work at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday morning to oversee training with the players who are not away on international duty amid increasing uncertainty over his position after ten months in charge.

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their third permanent head coach this year after he replaced Ruben Amorim in January.

It’s unclear what would happen to his backroom staff. Goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson was already at the club when Carrick arrived and would be likely to stay, along with Travis Binnion who moved up to first-team coach after working with United’s age-group teams.

Jonny Evans had just left his role as loans manager, but returned to work alongside his old United teammate as part of a new coaching team that includes Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate.

Carrick was only handed a two-year contract in May and would be due a pay-off from United who have already spent £22.7million in compensation since 2024 under Ineos.

It includes £10.4million to Erik ten Hag and his staff when the Dutchman was sacked four months after being given a contract extension, £4.1million to Dan Ashworth who lasted just 159 days as sporting director, and £8.2million to Amorim and his backroom team when they left after 14 months.

It would have been as high as £16.7million but United saved half of that figure when the Portuguese coach returned to work at AC Milan.

Avram Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, co-owners, are pictured at Old Trafford in September

Pochettino was strongly linked with the United job before the club appointed Ten Hag in 2022 and again when he was under pressure two years later.

The 54-year-old is currently busy at the US national team base south of Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double-header against Haiti.

However, it’s known that Pochettino would be interested in a return to the Premier League where he previously worked at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton.

#1845. How to watch Germany vs Netherlands: TV channel and live stream for Nations League today

Nations League fates will be decided this evening as Germany and the Netherlands face off in a mouth-watering showdown between two European heavyweights.

Both teams are largely in control of their own destiny, though a draw would certainly suit the Dutch more as it would be enough to top Group A2 and secure home advantage in the quarter-final second leg - which will be played in March 2027.

Germany, now managed by former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss Jurgen Klopp, can finish first but must beat the Netherlands and hope Greece fail to do so against a Serbia side that has lost all five matches thus far.

A point here for the Germans would leave qualification for the knockout phase hanging by a thread and they would be left relying on Serbia to beat Greece in Volos.

The reverse fixture between Germany and Netherlands finished all square in September as Cody Gakpo denied his former manager (Klopp) victory in his first game in charge of the national team with a 92nd minute equaliser in Amsterdam.

The Dutch have gone on to win three times since, including a 7-0 thumping of Greece on Friday night, but are without a win over Germany since September 2019.

#1843. Manchester United hounded off pitch by own fans

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

Brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

“We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y

2 league one teams and 13 premier league teams in a cup draw.. You couldn't write it Ridiculous 😡😡😡I give up on cup draws after 20 years waiting for one 😂

I think we’ve got to be a little bit careful on that one. He’s a 15-year-old boy. It’s more about the welfare and the care of JJ as a child really, or certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we’ve got to be a little bit careful of the exposure and how we jump on that.

The start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a big way.

There’s a number of things we’ll look at, we’ll dissect and I know quite a bit of where it went wrong. We can’t accept that as a group. I take responsibility, the performance towards the second half that’s on me. We’ll have to get better, we have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to get back to winning football matches.

We’ve got to keep evolving as a group. We have to keep learning and dealing with situations. Sometimes they come a bit easier than others. Tonight was a tough one. We didn’t find a way out of it. That’s up to me and the staff to help the players and guide them through it. I think we all know that in the end tonight feels like a big disappointment.

We’ve had small, little things that have gone against us in the last week or two and then it accumulates to feel that it’s a lot bigger. I think we have to be honest and say that. The late goal against Everton from outside the box. The [Manchester] City goal the other day. It can all of a sudden roll into something a bit greater but I understand the disappointment because we shouldn’t finish the game in that manner with the position we were in and we have to be humble and take that.

Boos ring around Old Trafford. Manchester United are out of the Carabao Cup, but of greater significance is that this defeat continues a poor start to the season and a general mood of deflation around the club. For the first time in 50 years, they lose a game at Old Trafford after leading 2-0. Another proud record falls in the post-Ferguson era.

Brighton have now won five of their last six games at Old Trafford, and are one of the best front-footed sides in the league on form.

As United push everyone forward, Heaven is penalised for a push on Vuskovic, and that is surely that now.

Mbeumo tees up Fernandes for a Hail Mary from 25 yards but he balloons the shot miles over the bar. Brighton fans can see the finish line and a place in the fourth round now.

Five minutes of added time to play, but Brighton have a corner after their press ensnares Tielemans on the edge of United’s defensive third. Dalot got a toe to the ball to prevent Rutter a sight at goal. Darlow claims the delivery, but some time has ticked away.

Tielemans slices his cross over the bar while off balance. This would be the first time since 1976 that United have led 2-0 in a game at Old Trafford and gone on to lose. At the moment, an equaliser does not look to be on its way.

Old Trafford growing impatient with how slowly United are moving the ball, a lack of options for the player in possession and they are being caught on it repeatedly by a sharp Brighton team.

Diego Gomez really should have sealed the victory, picked out by another clever Gross pass, but with so much time to take aim he blasted straight at Darlow. United still alive in the tie, but only just.

Lovely Brighton interplay again, Gross just keeps making the right decision around the box. This time his cut-back finds Kostoulas but Yoro blocks his goal-bound shot. Now Brighton make their fifth change: Rutter replaces Kostoulas.

Brighton still swinging punches. Costinha swings in a teasing cross to the back post, headed down by Gross, but De Cuyper cannot get over his volley. Carrick has made his final change: Cunha is on for Rashford.

Big miss by Rashford, but a big save from Jason Steele. It was a lovely touch by Fernandes while half stumbling that released Rashford, and he had so much time to think when through against the goalkeeper, but Steele stuck out a right boot to save.

Hurzeler making two more Brighton changes: Ayari and Kadioglu on for Hadjam and Boscagli, which probably makes their XI on the pitch even stronger. Kadioglu was voted Brighton’s player of the season for 2025-26.

Bruno Fernandes is stripped and ready to come on, Carrick calling for the man he would rather was resting on the bench. Fernandes replaces Mount.

De Cuyper, only on for a few minutes, scores the goal, but it was the off-the-shoulder threat of Kostoulas that made the goal. It looked as if the striker had the ball stuck under his feet, but he squeezed in a low cross that deflected off Mazraoui into the path of De Cuyper who had the simplest of finishes.

Brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL

Changes all round: Mainoo, Mbeumo and Zirkzee replace Sesko, Lacey and Andrey Santos.

For Brighton: De Cuyper and Diego Gomez on for Yalouye and Matt O’Riley.

He has been the scourge of United on so many occasions, and so it has proved again. United tried to play out from deep against Brighton’s press, hooked a longer pass around the corner towards Sesko but Vuskovic nipped in front of him to win a booming header back to Gross at the edge of the box. Nice touch to shift the ball left, before finishing across Darlow.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060

Short corner from United after good work from Rashford, but Tielemans could not keep his curling shot under the bar. Brighton break, but it is better defending from Heaven against Kostoulas this time. Carrick is preparing a triple sub.

Sesko with space to drive forward and look to pass or shot, but he dallies and dawdles before losing possession, much to the frustration of Old Trafford. Sesko has looked short of sharpness and confidence so far.

Delicious pieces of skill from Lacey, a Cruyff turn against the touchline when he was facing away from goal. Hadjam thought he had the winger boxed in, and dragged him down at the expense of a yellow card. Crowd enjoyed that.

Vuskovic with a shot from distance which is always rising; a number of Brighton players have tried their luck from range tonight, perhaps inspired by Lewis Dunk’s screamer at Coventry. This second half has a been a bit of a non-event thus far.

Matt O’Riley clips Heaven, which enabled the United defender to get out jail because he did not have control of the ball and was scrambling. Then Struijk very nearly sells Steele short with a back pass, had Sesko have won the first touch it was a red card or a goal, but Steele went to ground to win the ball well outside his area.

Rashford has been a bright spark for United, but he is having to do too much of the heavy lifting on his own at the moment. This time he finds Lacey on the overlap, but his cross is volleyed clear. Moments before that, the Old Trafford crowd were unhappy that Lacey was not awarded a free-kick. Looked like Hadjam took a swipe.

Brighton continue to apply the squeeze, but Kostoulas fouls Mazraoui to enable Darlow to boot the ball long and United to push up the pitch. Carrick’s team are still not exerting much control on the contest, though.

That is something of a rarity at this stage of the League Cup.

Plenty of entertainment for the paying punters at Old Trafford, with Shea Lacey and Mason Mount scoring twice in two minutes to put United in a commanding position. Given the JJ Gabriel story, the home fans enjoyed seeing a 19-year-old kiss the badge after scoring on his full debut.

Brighton have probably been the better team in general play though, and scored a deserved goal on the stroke of half-time.

United’s second-string back four looking very shaky, understandably.

Carrick and United wanted a foul on Sesko on halfway, but the referee said nothing doing. Hadjam then floats a diagonal pass over the head of Heaven to find the run of Kostoulas, but goalkeeper Darlow surely had the chance to come off his line and claim? Passive goalkeeping, and Kostoulas slips the ball under Darlow into the far corner. Game on.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c

Chema Andres, signed by Brighton from Stuttgart on deadline day and known by the moniker “Baby Rodri”, has just been booked for a reckless challenge in midfield. Then Rashford shows he still has plenty in the locker with a touch and shimmy to beat Costinha.

Tielemans with an important challenge on Kostoulas, after more unconvincing United involving Dalot misjudging a bouncing ball. Then Kostoulas fizzes a cross all the way through the six-yard box and Gross fires over at the back post. Brighton have had the chances to be level.

Yalcouye was very dangerous for Brighton against Coventry, and he is proving difficult to contain again. Gross’s through ball releases him into space behind Dalot, but his side-footed shot was shoved wide of the post. He tried to “Henry” one around Darlow with his right instep and failed to find the curl.

Clean hit from almost 35 yards from Boscagli, but his left-footed attempt whistles just over the bar. Yoro heads away a temping Gross cross when Brighton had three blue shirts in promising positions. Rashford then puts the ball through the legs of Chema Andres, and United have a corner.

Lacey goes down hoping for free-kick, anticipating the contact from Gross but it was not forthcoming. Since 2013-14, United have been 2-0 up at Old Trafford 145 times, winning 143 and drawing just two.

Brighton well on top now, and Ayden Heaven goes to ground hoping for a free-kick but the referee is having none of it. O’Riley’s cross is turned behind for a corner, which United scramble away. Feels like a Brighton goal is on the way, despite the comfortable scoreline for United.

Brighton’s corner swung in from the right was far too deep and loopy, drifting harmlessly behind for a United goal kick. Brighton are soon back on the front foot, and Gross picks out Kostoulas in the middle but the forward’s touch let him down. Edgy defending from Yoro but United clear their lines eventually.

Mazraoui is now back on the pitch but he does not look 100 per cent. Brighton enjoying some long passages of possession now, but you sense United are happy to drop off and let them have the ball. More promising build-up play ends with Mazraoui heading a cross over the bar for a Brighton corner.

There has been a lengthy stoppage in play while Mazraoui receives treatment for a bang on the head. United’s left-back looks a little shaken and is off the pitch now, and Mason Mount has dropped into the left-back position.

Sesko and Vuskovic are enjoying a good battle early on. Andrey Santos then sells Tielemans a little short in midfield and Brighton take advantage, but O’Riley does not have the pace to get away from Mazraoui.

There are usually chances at both ends when Brighton are involved and so it has proved so far. A pleasant surprise for any Manchester United fans who feared the worst arriving at Old Trafford tonight.

Shea Lacey is the first teenager to score on their full Man Utd debut since Marcus Rashford back in 2016. And they even got to celebrate together 🥺 pic.twitter.com/hBeXpCr4Tc

Brighton playing their way into trouble in their own defensive third, and it is great work from Rashford to drive into the penalty area from the left. Steele makes a save with his feet, but the ball runs kindly for Mount to power his shot into the ground and into the roof of the net.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf

The 19-year-old, sent off against Brighton in the FA Cup last season, has powered a left-footed shot from the edge of the box beyond Steele. That is a moment to lift the Old Trafford crowd.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge

Really slick, one-touch football from Brighton through midfield, players bumping off passes blind around the corner knowing their team-mate has read the next move, but the move breaks down at the edge of the box. Brighton tend to have plenty of possession and they have made a confident start. Boscagli then tries to chip Darlow from about 70 yards but it was never really on.

Some sound early defending from Brighton right-back Constinha, just when it looked like Rashford was going to break into space down the left flank. Yalcouye with a flick around the corner in midfield but his touch gets away from him and he commits a foul.

Then Yalcouye’s directness causes Yoro a problem near the left touchline, with the French defender hacking him down.

Tonight promises to be a test for Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro who are a young centre-back partnership for United. Looks a good crowd for a third-round League Cup game.

Meanwhile, some interesting news on JJ Gabriel’s future from our man at Old Trafford:

Barcelona are leading the race for JJ Gabriel after the 15-year-old requested to quit Manchester United.

Telegraph Sport revealed this week that Gabriel has told the club he wants to cancel his registration and move as a free agent, with Europe’s biggest club well aware of the teenager.

Gabriel travelled to Barcelona last season when he was shown around their training ground and met Wojciech Szczesny and club legend Sergio Busquets.

Sources at rival Premier League suitors believe that Barça have stolen a march in the race for the England Under-17 forward.

Should he move abroad, United may only get around £300,000 in training compensation as Gabriel has a European Union passport.

United would be expected to look into whether there was any influence from football agents before September 1 when Gabriel was allowed to have a representative.

They are the Premier League’s top scorers with 13 goals in four games and they also lead the division when it comes to expected goals amassed. Brighton have also won four of their last five visits to Old Trafford in all competitions.

We’ve got the squad to do it, we feel its important and the boys are desperate to play. We’ve got a very good team out.

We’ve moved on [from the Manchester derby]. On the day, you have to deal with it, I think there’s been enough said about it [the VAR decision] and we move on.

They’re a very good team, the way they play, you make you work for it, we’ll be ready for that. They play some very good football, and score an awful lot of goals.

Youri Tielemans has been given the armband for the evening in an interesting Manchester United line-up named by Michael Carrick. Karl Darlow gets his club debut and Mason Mount is back from injury. Shea Lacey gets a start too, a home-grown talent given his chance in the week JJ Gabriel, 15, has requested to leave Old Trafford.

Eight changes by Carrick, with Karl Darlow between the sticks. Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven, Andrey Santos, Mount, Sesko and Lacey the other players to come in. No JJ Gabriel in the squad.

United starting XI: Darlow; Dalot, Yoro, Heaven, Mazraoui; Santos, Tielemans; Lacey, Mount, Rashford; Sesko.

Subs: Lammens, Maguire, Amass, Fernandes, Mainoo, T Fletcher, Cunha, Zirkzee, Mbeumo

Lewis Steele replaces Bart Verbruggen in goal, and O’Riley, Costinha, O’Riley, Chema and Hadjam are the other players to come in. With the Conference League not starting until after the international break, Brighton do not have a pressing need to rotate.

Brighton XI: Steele, Costinha Vuskovic, Struijk, Boscagli, Chema, Gross, O’Reilly, Yalcouye, Hadjam, Kostoulas

Subs: Verbruggen, Dunk, Georginio, Promise, Osman, Kadioglu, Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Our starting XI for #MUNBHA. 👊 pic.twitter.com/gK5tUVYJ7L

Talents like Gabriel offer United fans hope of a brighter future after years of failure and underachievement.

No one can be certain he will fulfil the vast potential everyone in football circles can see. But United would love to have a good stab at helping him realise it.

The notion of him doing it somewhere else will send chills down the spines of the Old Trafford hierarchy.

Here are the numbers. Man City vs Norwich is tomorrow night, so their last-16 tie will be clarified then. Spurs, Leeds and Forest three Premier League teams who have already fallen by the wayside.

The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears. Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1842. CM: Three names on the list as Milan begin difficult hunt for Modric’s heir

AC Milan must start thinking about the midfield of the future, and there are reportedly a few names on the list of ideas.

At 41 years of age Luka Modric, still remains simply irreplaceable for Ruben Amorim and for Milan. However, given that his deal expires at the end of the season, the Rossoneri management have a duty to also look to the future and prepare for the post-Modric era.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The scouting team are very active in England, Spain, Belgium, and France, looking for the right players for Amorim’s footballing philosophy. Among the priorities for next season is identifying the right player to potentially take the reins as a deeper-lying playmaker.

Calciomercato.com report that three players have attracted considerable interest from Milan. One of them is Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, but he remains a dream at the moment because Arsenal and Chelsea have already swooped in on him.

The 23-year-old was called up to the England squad for the last break because manager Thomas Tuchel is very keen on him, but there’s a significant obstacle: the price tag. In England, there is even talk of a €100m+ asking price, given the clubs interested.

The spotlight has recently turned on Brighton’s Yasin Ayari too. He’s a highly versatile midfielder, performing at a high level both as a defensive midfielder and behind the striker. The Swede’s deal runs out in 2027 making him a big opportunity, but Brighton have a one-year option to.

Finally, we arrive at the new name on the list: Adem Zorgane of Union-Saint Gilloise. Scouts like what they have seen from the Algerian, who combines physicality with good technical ability. He would likely be the cheapest of the three, but his potential is high in the eyes of Milan.

#1840. Ex-Premier League ref calls Mikel Arteta a ‘nightmare’ to deal with

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has named Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as the toughest person to deal with on the touchline.

Last month, Arteta received his second yellow card of the season during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton but said after the game that he had a dossier of other managers committing similar offences which have gone unpunished.

The Arsenal manager now faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives a third yellow card.

Scott, who refereed in the Premier League for a decade before retiring in 2025, claims Arteta ‘does push all the limits all of the time’ and described the Spaniard as ‘hard work’.

When asked who was the worst manager to deal with on the touchline, Scott told The Athletic: ‘Well, the trite answer is all of them when they’re losing.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The honest answer, I’m afraid, I know whatever I say at this point just gets me pelters but it is Arteta. He is the hardest work.

‘He really does push all the limits all of the time. I don’t mind that in many ways, he’s trying to get a competitive advantage for his team. That’s fine. That’s part of his job. And of course, he’s entitled to do it, and it’s for us to place them, but he does make your life extremely difficult.

‘He’s out of his box [technical area] all the time. I watched him recently in the game against Everton and every time Everton had the ball anywhere near the touchline on his side, he was like joining in the press, his toes are on the touchline.

‘As fourth official, it’s a nightmare, because if you step forward and do anything about it, you’re being pedantic, being petty. He does get away with rather too much. The officials do need to be a bit tighter. And I was one of them who let him do that. I’m not going to deny that. But he was just hard work. Really, really hard work all the time in a way that others tended to be hard work some of the time.

‘And let’s not pretend the others are all, by comparison, angelic. Some were very controlled. Graham Potter would be an example. Didn’t have anything to do with you, just very, very calm, quiet. But then, of course, he got some stick at times for not showing that he cared enough. So I guess managers can’t win either way.’

#1839. Martin Odegaard clarifies Arsenal future as Champions League club prepares shock move

Martin Odegaard hopes to stay at Arsenal ‘for a long time’ despite interest from Bayern Munich.

The Gunners captain has 18 months left on his current contract in north London. Arsenal are keen to agree an extension with the midfielder to prevent him entering the last 12 months of his deal.

Injury issues and inconsistent form raised questions over his long-term future at stages in north London last season.

But the skipper has returned to form this campaign, still one of Mikel Arteta’s first choice picks in midfield despite the intense competition for places.

While he remains a key figure at the Emirates, reports have suggested uncertainty over his contract situation has invited interest from elsewhere.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Sky Germany reported last month Bayern Munich have had ‘ongoing contact’ with Odegaard who would be open to joining the German giants if he were to leave Arsenal.

The report added the Premier League champions will consider a sale next summer if a new deal is not agreed, unwilling to risk losing him on a free transfer.

Speaking on international duty with Norway, Odegaard has said he has no immediate plans to leave Arsenal but admitted there have been no talks over a new contract yet.

‘I’m happy and hope I can stay there [at Arsenal] for a long time to come, but we haven’t started on that yet,’ Odegaard said when asked about his contract situation.

#1838. Pocognoli convinced Gannon-Doak is ready to take the next step after his impressive form for Bournemouth

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 10 November 2026

SCOTLAND boss Sebastien Pocognoli is confident Ben Gannon-Doak is ready to hit new heights with the national team after a good run of form at club level.

Gannon-Doak had been one of the players about whom Pocognoli expressed concerns over a lack of game time heading into the last international window.

But the 20-year-old winger has been getting more game time for Bournemouth over recent weeks, particularly in their Europa League campaign.

Gannon-Doak was man of the match a couple of weeks ago as Bournemouth battered AC Milan 3-0, an outstanding performance which caught Pocognoli’s eye.

Now heading into the final two Nations League fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland, the Scotland boss already views Gannon-Doak as a much-improved player.

Gannon-Doak leaves AC Milan defenders trailing in his wake in an impressive display

‘Ben’s intensity is totally different from when he arrived in the camp in La Manga (at the start of the last window),’ he said.

‘You saw his press against AC Milan or in the other Europa League games, it’s totally different fitness now.

‘I am very happy with him and I believe that if we are playing good football it doesn’t matter the shape, he’s in the best position.

‘He’s a young lad, twenty years old, so he needs confidence and to feel the love. He’s a top player and top players want to improve every day.

‘I like his mentality, it’s exciting to see it but what’s the most exciting is that he’s still to improve on many aspects of the game.

‘If he can improve on being more clinical in front of goal he would probably have scored two goals in the last camp.

‘His assists and crossing is more with the idea before like: “If I put a cross in, Scott McTominay will make a bicycle kick”.

‘But you see a little bit more of him thinking what the next action is when he’s dribbling. When he’s more efficient I think he will be a different level. But he’s only 20 years old so it’s quite exciting.’

The winger has been tipped to make a big impact for Scotland in the upcoming fixtures

Pocognoli had previously indicated that some players would struggle to be part of his squad moving forward unless they were playing regularly for their club sides.

A £25million signing at Bournemouth after leaving Liverpool, Gannon-Doak was chief among those players given that he had struggled to establish himself.

‘I said to the lads when they arrived in September there were a lot of players with a lack of minutes,’ continued Pocognoli.

‘I said that when European football arrives they’ll probably share it. I’m sure the camp we had allowed a lot of players to go back to their clubs to bounce.

‘If you compare it to the first camp, there are maybe only two or three players who have been playing less minutes but the rest have continued.

‘So I think the camp helped them build the confidence and get some minutes.’

Pocognoli will be looking to bounce back from the disappointment of the defeat to Slovenia at the end of the last camp which punctured a lot of the optimism around the national team.

Scott McTominay will now be back among the key players after he missed out last time around due to the fact he was recovering from a heart procedure.

Pocognoli has high hopes for Gannon-Doak, and will also welcome McTominay into the fold

On the chance to work with the Napoli midfielder, Pocognoli said: ‘I have a very good impression of him.

‘I can imagine the fans are really excited to see him back, it has been a long time since the World Cup. If I was him I’d be really excited.

‘We will try to have a game plan so he can shine and not be too dependent on what he can produce from an individual action.

‘I am really excited to see if it can work and what he can bring to the way we want to play.

‘It’s exciting. He missed the first camp but I was in contact with him.

‘He’s excited to start a new book and try to push the level higher, to be successful for the next tournament.

‘I think we can try to play like we showed in some moments in the last camp and I believe we can produce this in the long-term.

‘It would be a massive boost for maybe the way we can play in the future.

‘I hope we can be successful, maybe it will not but I believe we have all the qualities to do it, honestly.’

#1835. Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed ban for tackle that led to Jesus de Miguel death

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement said: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Speaking this week, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said that Owono is still considering his future in football.

‘He is deeply affected by the situation,’ Manso said.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’

Earlier this week, Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Owono is barely leaving his house following De Miguel’s death and is closely working with psychologists and doctors.
