#1834. Who will England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed after Spain win

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

England player ratings: Surprise Arsenal star scores 8/10 as huge statement issued

Ice warnings in force with motorists urged to take care

How to watch Germany vs Netherlands: TV channel and live stream

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s one confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent so far is Belgium after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 by France.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents will be revealed over the next couple of nights, but as things currently stand, they could be drawn against either Greece or Denmark.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1830. I've worked for 20 years to try and play at a World Cup... I was never going to let heart procedure get in the way of my dream, says McTominay

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:37 EST, 10 November 2026

AS he lay on a hospital bed in Boston, just 48 hours or so before the start of the World Cup back in the summer, Scott McTominay could easily have felt like his dream was being snatched away from him.

Having played such a key role in helping Scotland get back to the Promised Land after 28 years in exile, McTominay was about to go under an anaesthetic for a heart procedure.

The issue became known at Scotland’s training base in Charlotte. By the time the team had flown to Boston for the opening match against Haiti, it was a matter of urgency.

McTominay was taken straight from the airport to the hospital via a police escort. Nobody would have blamed him if football had been the last thing on his mind.

Nor would anyone have blamed him if he pulled out of the squad altogether. But, after talking it through with the doctors, nothing was more certain in his own mind than that he would play.

McTominay played in all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup despite the procedure

Yet, nonetheless, a very obvious question remained. Was there ever any concern from his family? Was there ever a feeling that sitting it out would be the safest course of action?

‘No, I wouldn’t have listened to it [if they had said that],’ explained the Scotland midfielder. ‘All my family and friends had just flown 10 hours for the first game of the World Cup.

‘I didn’t sit there thinking I might not play. That would never be the case. I was always going to play in that game. Maybe selfishly, I don’t know but that’s football.

‘Players play with injuries all the time when they’re not quite right and it might be to the detriment of the team. I was fully functional.

‘It was in my hands. The medical team reassured me it was safe to play and they said: "What do you think?" I said: "Let’s go for it".'

McTominay essentially needed the rhythm and beat of his heart to be reset.

The midfielder struggles during the 1-0 defeat to Morocco at Boston Stadium

Explaining the procedure in more detail, he said: ‘Atrial fibrillation is a fairly normal routine thing for people in general.

‘They might not know that they have it. But when you’re an elite athlete in general across the board, across football, across sports in general, you know if you’ve got something that’s different.

‘Whenever you’re running and you check your pulse and it’s got a slight irregular beat there, it feels like your heart’s coming out of your chest.

‘Not obviously as bad as that but that’s the sensation that you have that it’s pumping, but not a regular heartbeat that’s like: “Bum, bum, bum, bum”.

‘Mine’s going: “Bum, bu-bu-bum, bum, bu-bu-bum”. So you know the difference.

‘We went to Boston, we got a police escort to go and get the shock then that was it to be honest. After that, I was back in normal rhythm, which is how a healthy heart should be then I went and played the game two days later.

‘The heat was tough, that was probably the hardest part. But I’ve worked for 20 years as a young footballer and as a professional to get to that point. To try and play well at a World Cup.

‘If things were a bit different in the second or third game, you never know what might have happened.’

McTominay has been in fine form for Napoli this season following a further procedure

McTominay played in all three matches against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil as Scotland were knocked out at the group stage.

Many fans had questioned his form, along with other senior players like John McGinn and Andy Robertson, albeit completely oblivious to what was going on behind the scenes.

Asked for his overall reflections on the World Cup, the Napoli midfielder said: ‘It wasn’t easy. Probably two, three weeks of putting my head in the sand, thinking we let one slip. That was just the bottom line.

‘It took me longer than what I normally would do to get over disappointment in football, to know the reason why I felt like it was just because we could have done more.

‘But in general it was probably one of the worst moments of my career.

‘Then I had the surgery at the start of the season. It went well and there was no doubt in my mind I would come back from it.

‘After the operation, I had three weeks at home. I didn’t watch as much football as I normally do. Normally I watch games relentlessly every night.

‘So I had three weeks of resting my mind more than anything to try and come back in a better state. I’m feeling good now and looking forward to getting going again.’

McTominay eventually underwent corrective surgery back at the start of the season which ruled him out of Scotland’s opening four fixtures in the Nations League.

Now back on form for Napoli and back in the Scotland squad, he’s desperate to make an impact for Sebastien Pocognoli’s new-look side.

Scotland will face North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday night before rounding off their Nations League campaign with a trip to Switzerland.

So often Scotland's talisman, he has returned ahead of the Nations League double header

McTominay spoke highly of the new head coach and has been impressed by his methods in training so far this week.

‘I like it, I like his ideas a lot,’ he said of Scotland’s new boss. ‘Whenever I first had a meeting with him, I liked the way that he wants to play the game.

‘High energy, high tempo, and obviously different ideas tactically on how to build up and the high-pressure situations we’ll find ourselves in, going against teams and trying to nick it off them and create goals that way, which is another tool in how to score goals and put the ball in the back of the opposition’s net.

‘So yeah, the early signs are really good, and he’s a great guy as well, as are his staff. I’m looking forward to it.

‘I feel like I’m a young kid that is coming back to learn as much as possible, and to try and soak it all in and help the younger ones realise the opportunity that they have in Scotland and in football in general.

‘They don’t maybe realise how far they can push themselves to break boundaries and limits in the game, and that can really pay off.’

#1827. England: How many games Elliot Anderson will miss after Spain red card

Elliot Anderson is facing a suspension after being sent-off in England’s Nations League win over Spain.

Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White had the Three Lions cruising to victory at 3-0 on Sunday night, before Anderson’s challenge on Lamine Yamal produced both a red card and a penalty.

Mikel Oyarzabal successfully converted the spot-kick before substitute Nico Williams reduced deficit with 15 minutes plus stoppage time remaining.

Ultimately, England held on for a famous win and topped Group A3 as a result.

England will discover their quarter-final opponents later this week, but they will be without Anderson for the first-leg because of the red card.

UEFA rules stipulate “a player or team official sent off by the referee is automatically suspended for the next match in the competition.

“In the event of a serious offence, the UEFA disciplinary bodies are entitled to augment this punishment, including by extending it to other competitions.”

Due to Anderson being given his marching orders in the Spanish capital for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity, rather than violent conduct, his punishment will be a one-game ban.

Therefore, the Manchester City midfielder will be available for the second leg in March 2027 - if named in the England squad by Thomas Tuchel.

Tuchel, meanwhile, slammed the decision as a ‘double punishment’ during his post-match press conference, dissecting a classic England performance after becoming the first team to beat Spain in 43 competitive matches.

Tuchel commented: “The red card and the penalty is always a big decision - and I need to understand why it's a double punishment.

"Then it was a long, long 30 minutes - but I don't want to focus on that. There was so, so many positive things about the result after 60 minutes. It was well deserved.”

The England manager also made reference to his side’s performance with 10 men during the World Cup, when the Three Lions held on after a red card against hosts Mexico to win 3-2 in the round of 16.

"For me, the red card was more like the Azteca reloaded,” continued Tuchel.

"Against this team half an hour feels like two hours. Full of quality. You can see the second goal coming and it's a long, long time to overcome it. That's the way it is.

"We showed that without the red card, we had a clear win. Brilliant performance overall. We were the better team. We put out a fantastic performance from start to finish.”

#1826. Tottenham urged to consider shock transfer move for £64m Arsenal star

Tottenham should consider a shock transfer move for out-of-favour Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres, according to former manager David Pleat.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side won three of their four matches prior to the international break to move up to 11th in the Premier League table.

Despite their lavish summer spending, Spurs still lack a reliable goalscorer, with centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke the only player to have scored more than one league goal so far this season.

And while he is not blown away by the options on the market, Pleat suggested that Spurs look to their arch-rivals for a solution to their lack of goal-scoring threat.

‘There aren’t many out there, there’s a very small amount of strikers,’ he told The Last Word On Spurs.

‘Are you going to buy Lankshear back now for £50 million? He’s the top scorer in the Championship, our boy.

‘So where are you going to get? Are Arsenal going to give us someone like Jesus, or someone they don’t want? He’s gone already, but, Gyokeres, perhaps. Who else is there?’

‘[Brian] Brobbey gave us trouble… [Dominic] Calvert-Lewin is very good in the air but had injury problems.

‘When you are signing a striker, it’s about what type of striker. Is he exceptionally good in the air, is he a bully-type striker like Delap or is a clever front player, more like Havertz.’

Gyokeres arrived for big money from Sporting CP last season, but has started just one league match this campaign after falling beneath Kai Havertz in the pecking order.

But despite his lack of starts, Gyokeres insisted he has no desire to leave Arsenal as speculation mounts ahead of the January transfer window.

‘I want to [stay],’ he told reporters while away on international duty with Sweden. ‘It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup [Fleetwood].

‘Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

‘The communication with Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.’

#1825. ‘Next star’ – Mauricio Pochettino tipped to sign £67m target for Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino has been tipped to complete the marquee signing of Como midfielder Nico Paz for Manchester United.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half year deal in Manchester and will join up with the squad ahead of their trip to Anfield to face Liverpool next Sunday.

United have made their worst start to a season in 40 years, and are currently without a league win since mid-August.

As he looks to arrest that slide, Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as United look to fill gaping holes in their squad at left-back and forward areas.

But former Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor believes Pochettino may also look to move on senior players and earmarked Bruno Fernandes as one who might have an uncertain future under the Argentine.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Fernandes’ contract is up at the end of the season, with recent reports suggesting that the Red Devils captain has rejected a second contract offer from the club.

And speaking on talkSPORT, Agbonlahor mused: ‘Maybe Pochettino comes in and says, “You know what? I don’t like his attitude. I don’t like the way he throws his arms up at his teammates, the way he threw Michael Carrick under the bus. Can I go and get my own players?”‘

Should Fernandes leave the club, Agbonlahor earmarked Como midfielder Paz as the perfect candidate to ‘refresh’ United’s squad.

‘Nico Paz – how good has he been?’ he added. ‘He’s the next star for Argentina.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Does Pochettino say, “You know what? I want him next summer from Como, make it happen”. Save the money on wages that maybe Bruno Fernandes wants.

‘So he might have his own ideas to get all these players out that maybe have been a little bit of a problem and to refresh the whole squad.’

Paz tormented Michael Carrick’s side in the Champions League last month, scoring twice and providing an assist in a 4-1 victory, having grown into one of Serie A’s brightest talents under Cesc Fabregas.

The Argentine joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid, although Los Blancos do retain a £67million buy-back clause, which can be activated next summer.

Recent reports in Spain indicate that the possibility of a move to the Premier League appeals to Paz’s representatives, although Como’s transfer position and Real’s intentions will be a deciding factor.

#1824. ‘Exposed the world champions’: Spanish press react to England win in Nations League

10 man England secured a miraculous 3-2 win against world champions Spain in Madrid to top their Nations League group.

The Three Lions raced into a 3-0 lead at the Metropolitano Stadium, before Elliot Anderson conceded a penalty and was shown a straight red card for bringing down Lamine Yamal inside the area.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored the resulting spot-kick, and substitute Nico Williams set up a nervy finish as he slotted the ball home after a quick counter-attack.

Despite late pressure from Spain, England held on thanks to a superb double save from James Trafford, ending La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run on a memorable night for Thomas Tuchel’s side.

Sunday’s result will go down as one of the most remarkable nights in England’s recent history, with Tuchel admitting his team reached the “highest level football-wise in all aspects of the game”.

Meanwhile, captain Harry Kane, who opened the scoring from the penalty spot at the end of the first half, said the victory was “as big as it gets” outside of a major tournament.

England entered the international break still carrying the scars of the World Cup, with Tuchel facing significant criticism for his in-game management during their semi-final defeat to Argentina.

However, victory over Spain means England have now won five of their six matches since returning from America, while Tuchel can point to having got his substitutions right as his side held on with 10 men to beat the reigning world and European champions in their own backyard.

England made the perfect start in the Spanish capital, with Declan Rice claiming post-match that, “The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played” as Luis de La Fuente’s side struggled to live with England’s pressing.

ITV pundit and former Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane was similarly impressed by England’s intense start, describing their first-half performance as “perfect” after Kane gave the visitors a deserved lead just before the break.

Keane’s ITV colleague, Ian Wright, was particularly pleased for Arsenal right-back Ben White, who was subjected to boos during England’s 2-1 victory over Croatia but started and scored against Spain after a flowing passing move.

“Can I just say, I’m really pleased for Ben White and the way things have turned around for him. It’s just brilliant for him to get back in, and he was magnificent tonight,” Wright said.

“Not just with the goal, but he was making tackles, niggling the Spain players. I’m so pleased it’s ended that way for him.

“There was a lot to be excited about for England. They were 3-0 up and cruising against the world champions before the red kind of changed the game.”

Spanish outlet AS also heaped praise on England’s performance, declaring the result as “the biggest setback of the De la Fuente era” with Tuchel’s men “completely neutralising Spain.”

“England exposed the world champions in what represents the biggest setback of the De la Fuente era, a bitter end to a dream 2026. Goals from Kane, Konsa, and White rewarded a superior opponent,” a report in AS stated.

“Tuchel’s men had managed to cut off both of their opponents’ cables, the red and the blue, completely neutralising Spain.”

England exposed the world champions in what represents the biggest setback of the De la Fuente era

Fellow Spanish outlet MARCA also chose to celebrate England’s dominance rather than attack Spain’s performance.

“It’s better to lose against a formidable opponent like England, who dominated the match until they were reduced to ten men,” MARCA said before continuing by lavishing praise on Tuchel.

“Credit goes to Tuchel, though his performance has been questioned because he seemed afraid to be the hero in the World Cup match against Argentina. It’s been a long time since an opponent has so thoroughly dismantled Spain.”

#1823. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1822. Erling Haaland speaks out on Manchester City future as financial scandal rumbles on

Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Manchester City’s players have not said much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, says he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything.’

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’

#1821. “Support Amorim and the players” – Pellegatti outlines Krösche’s important double role

Carlo Pellegatti has confirmed that Markus Krösche is on his way to AC Milan, and believes he will take up an important double role.

It is no secret that Milan have pursued Krösche for some time. There was an initial attempt to poach him in the summer to work alongside Ruben Amorim, the head coach he reportedly approved of hiring. However, Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall that proved too strong to break down.

After the summer window, the Bundesliga club confirmed that Krösche had left his position. The German director spoke about the desire to try something new, and sure enough the Milan rumours once again went into overdrive.

Based on what reliable sources are reporting, only the official announcement is missing with everything agreed. Carlo Pellegatti spoke in his column for MilanNews about what the hire should mean, for Amorim too.

“The arrival of Markus Krosche, a key figure in Eintracht Frankfurt’s recent successes, is expected towards the end of November,” the journalist began.

#1820. Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after criticism from Liverpool legend

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness said on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Declan Rice hit TWO worldie free-kicks vs Real Madrid 🤯So nice he did it twice ✌️ pic.twitter.com/zg5CzlQQNh

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

#1819. England winners and losers: Arsenal star rebuilding as Chelsea man suffers further setback

A terrific week for England ended with an away victory over Spain which Thomas Tuchel described as “like the Azteca reloaded”.

The Three Lions closed out their 2026 campaign by finishing top of their Nations League group thanks to a 2-1 win over Croatia last Thursday and then a heroic 10-man win in Madrid, 3-2, on Sunday.

While plenty of Tuchel’s players pushed their cases for further England involvement down the line, there were others who will feel less positive about the past week in terms of what it means for them.

Here, Standard Sport considers the winners and losers from England’s impressive autumn week.

Ben White has scored only 12 goals in his senior career but two have been for England, including the eventual winner in a famous win in Madrid.

Five years after his England debut, his first competitive start for his country came in Spain, and he didn’t disappoint.

The Arsenal man followed up a cameo against Croatia with one of England’s standout performances at the Estadio Metropolitano, defending robustly against Spain’s attacks down the left and then chipping in with that overlapping run and finish to make it 3-0.

Has had to field booing from sections of England fans since his return to the international fold in March after he walked away from their World Cup squad in 2022, but is rebuilding his England career successfully and will be thought of by Tuchel as one of his most well-balanced right-back options now.

Hopes to climb above Reece James and become first choice.

England’s left-back position changed hands a few times during the World Cup as Nico O’Reilly and Djed Spence battled it out mid-tournament, but that only served to make Tuchel’s decision to leave Hall behind appear all the more strange.

Hall has come back stronger and this month backed up his encouraging displays from the last international break.

Solid in the 2-1 win over Croatia, he was on another level entirely in Madrid, taking care of the threat of Lamine Yamal and finding a perfect balance between defence and attack as he helped England to victory in the world champions’ own backyard.

At the end of the last international break, when Trafford and Jordan Pickford split the four games two each, Pickford could no longer claim to be uncontested as England No1.

And after his heroics in Spain, even more so there is a debate to be had over whether it is time for England’s first-choice goalkeeper to be Leeds United’s Trafford rather than his Everton counterpart.

Pickford has never let England down in 94 caps, but Trafford made a string of stellar saves in Madrid and is eight years his junior.

Tuchel will likely continue to share the game time between them until he is pulled strongly enough in either direction. Trafford is making a very strong case for Pickford’s nine years without a genuine challenger to end with the shirt changing hands.

The Bayer Leverkusen defender has become accustomed to the bulk of his England game time being at right-back during this calendar year, but a shortage of centre-back options this month saw him start in the middle in both games

Quansah was solid for the most part but switched off in both games. And both errors were punished.

First he attempted a header back to Pickford from a Croatia corner that gifted the visitors a leveller at Wembley, then he dawdled on the ball long enough for Spain to intercept and race through; Elliot Anderson’s last-man red card and a Spain penalty followed.

Tuchel will hope he is stronger for the mistakes he made, but 23-year-old Quansah will be disappointed as he heads back to Germany.

Arguably it is harsh to include a player who was not even involved in the two matches, but the reason for Cole Palmer’s absence this month spoke volumes.

After dropping out of the last camp due to load management and being told by Tuchel that he “misses too many opportunities” to play for his country, this time the Chelsea talisman was not even selected.

Already faces huge competition in the No10 role but now there seems to be something of a repair job required if he is to get back into the fold and into Tuchel’s plans.

The 28-year-old is approaching 40 caps but his England career has been a strange old saga, really. Only Lee Carsley has ever appeared to truly trust him; Gareth Southgate and now Tuchel, less so.

Not in favour at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho, his England game time across the autumn has felt a result of Reece James’s injuries and evidence right-back is a problem position more than it has an opportunity earned through strong club form.

Categorising Alexander-Arnold as a sublime passer who is suspect defensively became cliché long ago — yet being pinched of the ball in a poor area by Croatia was just the latest confirmation.

England managers have lacked the faith required to start him in England’s toughest matches for years now, and so it continued as he remained an unused substitute in Madrid.

White is just the latest player to climb above him in the pecking order.

#1818. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of Man Utd mission

Mauricio Pochettino would welcome the chance to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares for the task of resurrecting Manchester United.

Michael Carrick’s successor’s penultimate match in charge of United States ended in an emphatic 6-0 thrashing of Haiti as he moved a step closer to beginning his United tenure.

The former Tottenham boss will start life at the Red Devils on Wednesday after two Nations League matches with Haiti, but USA all but assured their place in the semi-finals of the competition with a comprehensive first-leg showing.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The 54-year-old will have little time to reflect on his accomplishments in his soon-to-be former role as he will immediately begin plotting for his first game in charge of United at Anfield next Sunday.

Pochettino inherits a side that is currently in the bottom three in the Premier League table, short on confidence and a dressing room split following the recent actions of senior players, including the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez.

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’

Bruno Fernandes will delay any decision on a new Manchester United contract until he has made up his mind on new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

#1816. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the five teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, as things currently stand, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

Portugal’s position in Group A4 is still to be confirmed after they were humbled at home by Denmark in their first game since Cristano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1815. Mauricio Pochettino is adored by his players, big on culture and good vibes, not afraid to crack the whip and does not suffer fools - exactly what dysfunctional Man United are crying out for

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER and MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:59 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 10 November 2026

After one press conference during Mauricio Pochettino’s ill-fated spell at Chelsea, he hosted an Argentinian-style BBQ for approximately 130 people, including his players and their families, under a marquee set up in the first-team car park at their training ground.

Returning to the room and the assembled throng of journalists still working, Pochettino popped a large plate of sausages and steaks down on the desk. He insisted it did not constitute bribery for better coverage of him. Just thought we might like to join.

This was Pochettino personified. Big on togetherness. Insisted on creating a homely environment for everyone. Believed a harmonious culture at Cobham would help performances on the pitch. Even kept a big box of lemons in his office because he reckoned they harnessed ‘energia universal’. He emphasised the importance of a good mood.

Goodness knows that’s what Manchester United need right now. And if they do decide to dismiss Michael Carrick, the prospect of managing possibly the biggest club in world football would not faze Pochettino – now the bookies’ favourite to take over.

Indeed, the 54-year-old would relish the challenge.

A few days before USA’s World Cup victory against Bosnia and Herzegovina to reach the last 16 at this summer’s tournament, coach Pochettino invited a small group of journalists to interview him at the team hotel – the Ritz-Carlton in Laguna Niguel, overlooking the Pacific Ocean 50 miles south of Los Angeles.

Manchester United could do with a dose of Mauricio Pochettino - and he would relish the challenge

The United States manager - who would cost around £7.5million to release - has openly admitted he wants to lead them in the future

Towards the end of the interview the Manchester United job came up in conversation. Pochettino turned to his long-time assistant coach Jesus Perez and said: ‘One day, your dream comes true... you go to Manchester United!’.

The Argentine clarified somewhat by explaining that Perez, while living in London, would often visit Manchester on days off to visit the National Football Museum. Perez responded with a smile: ‘United should have got you’.

One thing about Pochettino that Manchester United players will soon figure out if he takes the reins at Old Trafford is that he is not afraid to crack the whip and does not suffer fools. At the World Cup, he appeared to criticise the intervention of FIFA - and President Trump – in suspending Folarin Balogun’s ban to make the striker available for a knockout clash with Belgium.

‘I feel disappointed with too many people. They put politics and manipulation, talk about ethics and integrity [first]. If we talk about the history of this game, I am disappointed in a personal way.’

With Pochettino, you’re either all in or you’re out. Look back to his time at Tottenham for evidence of that: the decision to exile stars such as Younes Kaboul, Etienne Capoue and Paulinho into a ‘bomb squad’ - and give chances to stars such as Harry Kane - was the start of his success there.

He’s a builder of teams, works with the tools he has and makes players better. Again, that sounds like the sort of thing United are crying out for.

Pochettino is big on culture – he adopted the mantra ‘culture eats strategy for breakfast’ after a meeting with the chairman of U.S. fast food chain Chick-fil-A – and worked hard to change the holiday camp feel at the USA team. Senior stars believed they did not need to put in the extra work to keep their places. The most notable example saw national team poster-boy Christian Pulisic, once of Chelsea, attempt to skip key games after a long season for AC Milan. Pochettino put a stop to that.

The Argentine does not suffer fools, is big on culture, and can deal with big club executives - his time at Tottenham taught us that

He can manage upwards, too. He handled chairman Daniel Levy well, and credited open dialogue as being key to the partnership with the chairman which yielded a runners-up finish in the Premier League and a run to the Champions League final.

‘I speak to him a lot, we talk a lot, we have very good communication,’ Pochettino said in 2018.

‘That means sometimes we agree and sometimes we don't agree. But after, when the decision is made, we are so strong in the delivery of it which shows it is best for the club’.

His cordial relationship with Levy meant Spurs were unconcerned when he met Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016 at Scott’s in Mayfair towards the end of Louis van Gaal’s troubled reign at Old Trafford.

There was nothing untoward in that - after the restaurant meeting Pochettino returned to Spurs training, and United appointed Jose Mourinho that summer.

But he was again touted as a contender when Mourinho was dismissed two years later.

Levy sacked him in 2019, but Pochettino has remained respectful and has since praised Levy’s impact.

On the field, his time at Spurs became famous for relentless intensity - a high energy approach with a high press. Think flying full-backs Danny Rose and Kyle Walker, and all-action midfielder Mousa Dembele. For another example of him getting the best from players look at Cole Palmer. The Englishman has never since replicated his numbers from 2023-24, Pochettino’s only season at Stamford Bridge.

The football, admittedly, was a little chaotic at Chelsea. It lacked control, and not even a mountain of meat could prevent him from being quizzed about his style of play in press conferences.

Chelsea’s fans never took to Pochettino. He was the face of Spurs, after all. Pochettino might be walking his dog – a Rhodesian Ridgeback called Sansa, named after the Game of Thrones character Sansa Stark – and the odd supporter would happily stop him to have a cosy chat. But he was always going to struggle to win over the supporters in their entirety.

He once said the first time he felt a connection with Chelsea’s supporters was in April 2024 after defeating Erik Ten Hag’s United 4-3, when Cole Palmer scored twice in the 10th and 11th minutes of stoppage time. That was 11 months after he joined.

He never quite won over the fanbase of Chelsea, where his football was chaotic and his high-intensity values led to accusations that he had worsened their injury crisis

One source at the time said Pochettino wanted ‘machines’ who had the physicality to play the high-energy philosophy he craved, and like at Spurs there was indeed a great deal of high-intensity running involved in training.

However, this talk of his sessions being fitness-focused led to accusations that his methods were contributing to their crippling injury list. Pochettino disputed that, telling us he did not come ‘from Mars’ and that he knew how to manage footballers better than those on social media. He was extremely defensive whenever asked if his training was primitive.

It would be fair to debate whether United have the players to play this way – and indeed how Pochettino himself would respond to the changing landscape of the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi noted recently that upon his return to the Premier League after two years away that almost all clubs now play a more physical game than when he was at Brighton. With more teams doing the same thing that once made a Pochettino side different, how would he adapt?

We are told leaving his job in charge of the USA is more contractually feasible now than it was before the 2026 World Cup when Spurs made checks last season. He has a buyout clause, apparently worth around £7million, though that does not include the compensation required to recruit Perez and Co.

Should United require any character references, they need only ask their own Luke Shaw. He wrote the epilogue of Guillem Balague’s book Brave New World: Inside Pochettino’s Spurs, having played under him at Southampton. Shaw admitted in those pages that he would love to work with his old coach again someday. Pochettino was there for him when Shaw broke his leg – still a man-manager even when they were no longer working together.

But United could also ask any number of Chelsea players who worked with Pochettino. They largely loved him. At the time of his dismissal in May 2024, one agent of a senior figure in the changing room told us that their client was ‘devastated’. Nicolas Jackson, formerly of Chelsea and now of Aston Villa, responded to Pochettino leaving by posting two face-palm emojis on Instagram.

Pochettino had his favourites. Conor Gallagher was one of them, and the Cobham graduate's contractual situation seemed to be a source of angst between the coach and Chelsea’s hierarchy.

Players tend to love Pochettino - Luke Shaw (right), one of Manchester United's veterans, had a strong relationship with him at Southampton

His power waned at Chelsea - the club hired a set-piece coach after he insisted he didn't want one, and he was gone before the specialist arrived

As noted, Pochettino was a builder hired to work with one of the Premier League’s youngest squads but did not get the time he wanted to mould Chelsea and never hid his desire for more power at Stamford Bridge. It is said they once had the chance to sign Ansu Fati from Barcelona on favourable financial terms, but did not go through with the transfer after the manager decided he was not for him.

We did get a glimpse of Pochettino’s waning power when Daily Mail Sport asked him once whether he would like a set-piece specialist adding to his staff. He dismissed the idea, suggesting he did not need one. Chelsea then lost the Carabao Cup final when Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk headed in the winner in extra time from a corner, with Gary Neville coining the ‘blue billion-pound bottlejobs’ jibe.

A month later, Chelsea agreed a deal to hire Bernardo Cueva from Brentford to lead a new department dedicated to set-pieces. Pochettino responded by reminding us: ‘I am the head coach and I am going to decide if some people are going to be with me or not, or if I’m going to add more people or not to the touchline.’ He was gone before Cueva arrived in the summer.

An end-of-season review was held in May 2024, and Pochettino, along with Chelsea’s hierarchy, decided after a single season that it was not working. Not for him, and not for them.

Now those at the helm of United need to determine whether he is the man to bring the good vibes back, perhaps also with a little meat.

#1814. Norway manager explains reason for ‘terribly tame’ Martin Odegaard performance

Arsenal skipper Martin Odegaard was accused of delivering a ‘terribly tame’ performance for Norway in their Nations League win over Wales.

The Gunners’ captian completed 90 minutes as Stale Solbakken’s side ran out comfortable 3-1 winners courtesy of goals from Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland.

Odegaard, however, appeared far from his usual energetic self and his lack of spark was noted by former Norway international Kjetil Rekdal.

‘I think he was terribly tame today,’ Rekdal told TV 2. ‘He looked tired and didn’t have the movement he usually has.

‘I think he was much less visible than he usually is.’

Solbakken, however, explained that his inspirational playmaker overcame an illness that caused Odegaard to endure a sleepless night prior to the match.

‘We have had a captain who has been lying around all night and spitting, and who was allowed to take some other liberties than he was supposed to,’ he said.

‘If you lie down all night and throw up, that’s it. All credit to him for going the distance. We had a conversation during the break that he should just drive from the start and let us know when the tank was empty.’

Odegaard’s commitment to the cause was praised by several of his teammates, including David Moller Wolfe.

Patrick Berg star, who started on the bench, but came on in the second half, added: ‘I understood that Martin had a bad night.

#1813. Emotional Massaro pays tribute to Baresi: “Every day it’s harder and harder”

Daniele Massaro has spoken about how much Franco Baresi meant to him, and how much he now misses the AC Milan icon.

The incredibly sad news broke over the summer that Baresi had passed away following a battle with illness. Thousands of fans lined the streets to pay tribute at his funeral, while the club have honoured him in several ways, including in the first home game against Venezia.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Given his importance to Milan both as a player and then as an ambassador, it has left a huge hole in the hearts of many, above all his former team-mates and colleagues who shared a dressing room and/or an office with him for many years.

At the presentation of Mauro Suma’s book ‘Il Milan nel Mondo’ many former players spoke, including Daniele Massaro. He was visibly emotional during his speech, admitting it is actually getting harder to arrive at work each day and not have Baresi there.

“It was something rare in football. For me every day it’s harder and harder to walk into the office where he used to sit, I miss him. Franco will always be a part of me,” he said.

“I was lucky enough to meet him as an opponent one of the few times we played against each other in Serie B with Monza, then in ’82 we played in the World Cup together. At Milanello I would get changed in front of him, it seemed unreal.”

#1812. Watch: Arsenal star Ben White confronted amid heated tunnel bust-up during Spain vs England

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal stars found themselves at the centre of a dispute as England and Spain players clashed at half-time of their Nations League showdown.

Gunners defensive duo Ben White and Ezri Konsa were on the scoresheet for the Three Lions, helping their side to a famous 3-2 win away in Spain.

England, however, had to see out the final 30 minutes with a man disadvantage as Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson was shown a red card for fouling Lamine Yamal inside the box.

Despite that, Thomas Tuchel’s side held on for three points that lifted them above Spain in their Nations League group.

The other major talking point in the Spanish capital was an incident that occurred at half-time, when White clashed with Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz as the pair walked off the pitch.

This lead to a pouring of white and red shirts. David Raya, back-up to Unai Simon while on international duty, joined Arsenal team-mate Konsa in calming matters.

Martin Zubimendi also attempted to play peacemaker after initially getting involved, conversing with Konsa as the huddle moved towards the tunnel.

A sixth Arsenal player was close by, as Mikel Merino - moments away from being hauled off at half-time - watched on as the argument fizzled out.

There were a total of eight Arsenal players involved in the matchday squads for both nations. Eberechi Eze was an unused sub on the England bench, with his club teammate Myles Lewis-Skelly introduced in the second half as Tuchel looked to see out victory for the Three Lions.

Arsenal wingers Noni Madueke and Bukayo Saka are England regulars, but missed out on the squad for the last international break of 2026.

The Gunners return to action this weekend, when they travel to face Newcastle on Saturday, November 21.

#1811. USA star lifts lid on Mauricio Pochettio approach that will delight Man Utd fans

USA defender Auston Trusty revealed the mindset Mauricio Pochettino has brought to the USMNT and Manchester United fans will like the sound of it.

Pochettino has been confirmed as the new manager of the Red Devils, but is finishing off his stint in charge of USA before travelling to Manchester.

On Saturday the Americans hammered Haiti 6-0 in Miami, before Pochettino’s last game at the helm against the same opponents in Cincinnati on Wednesday.

Celtic defender Trusty opened the scoring on Saturday and was full of praise for his outgoing Manchester.

The 28-year-old says the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss insists it is important for his team to keep pushing for more goals regardless of the scoreline, which is the kind of approach that will go down well at Old Trafford.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We play for him. Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously, it’s sad that he’s moving on. So it’s a great opportunity that he is moving on into,’ Trusty told TNT Sports after the win over Haiti.

‘But we play for him. It’s his team, it’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match, and no matter the opponent, no matter how many goals you’re up, you keep fighting, you keep putting on the score and just do your thing, play your game.’

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun also scored on Saturday and feels Pochettino has left the US team in great shape.

#1809. Spain boss Luis de la Fuente issues warning after Nations League defeat to England

Luis de la Fuente has stated the “best is yet to come” from Spain following their loss to England.

England’s 3-2 victory away in Madrid on Sunday evening ended Spain’s run of 43 straight games without defeat, handing the World Cup winners their first loss since March 2024.

Under De La Fuente, Spain have won a European Championship, a World Cup and a Nations League title in 2023 - as well as reaching the final of the latter in 2025.

However, defeat to England means that Spain will enter the quarter-finals stage of the 2026-27 Nations League as an unseeded runner-up, potentially setting up a showdown with France in March next year.

Reflecting on the game, De La Fuente said: “In the first 30 minutes, they knocked us out of our rhythm and were better than us. After that, we fought back, and I thought we were going to get the draw.

“But I’ll use a phrase that I’ve used before when we were unbeaten: ‘The best is yet to come’.”

De La Fuente also shared his belief that England approached the game in Madrid as a ‘final’, with Spain not as motivated for the game - which allowed the Three Lions to ‘trample’ over La Roja.

"The fact that the whole world wants to beat Spain is a great feeling,” he added. “This was a 'final', and in this type of game, you have to be spot on, in great shape, and if not, then an opponent like England, France, Portugal or Italy can trample all over you.”

The Spanish head coach went on to state that his side’s ambitions of winning the Nations League remained in place, with his side ‘determined’ to make amends.

He continued: "We'll try to be exactly the same in defeat as we were in victory. Okay, we haven't often tasted defeat, but we stay proud; we stay determined - in March, we're in the quarter-finals, and we'll go to those knockouts with the intention of winning, and winning the tournament."

#1808. Ian Wright praises ‘magnificent’ Arsenal star after England beat Spain

Ian Wright praised ‘magnificent’ Arsenal defender Ben White after England’s thrilling Nations League win over World Cup holders Spain.

England ended Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday evening.

The Three Lions were bright from the start and took the lead on the stroke of half-time through a penalty from England record goalscorer and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Ezri Konsa headed in Declan Rice’s corner shortly after the interval and England were in dreamland when White added a third on the hour mark, arriving at the back-post and firing past Unai Simon.

Spain were being outplayed but had renewed hope when Elliot Anderson was sent off for bringing down Lamine Yamal as he raced through on goal and Mikel Oyarzabal converted the subsequent penalty.

England fans were having flashbacks of last summer’s World Cup semi-final collapse against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second to set up a tense final 20 minutes.

The hosts pressed for an equaliser but were denied by some valiant England defending and an impressive display from goalkeeper James Trafford.

The hard-fought win means England, already through to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, finish top of their group ahead of World Cup holders Spain.

Wright felt England ‘deserved’ the win despite the late pressure from Spain and singled out Arsenal star White for special praise.
